text:
November 14, 1751. About 320 men held a half-ruined fort in southern India against roughly 11,000, and the attack broke when armoured war elephants were driven back by musket fire and trampled the men behind them.

The commander was a 26-year-old former East India Company clerk named Robert Clive, and that fifty-day siege is where British India begins.

The setting is the Carnatic, where the Mughal Empire's authority had become nominal and regional rulers fought over successions. Both the French and the British East India Companies had worked out that backing a claimant was cheaper than conquest and more profitable than trade alone.

Dupleix, the French governor, had spent the years after 1748 making the French the dominant European power in southern India. When Boscawen's British fleet left in 1749, the French effectively ran the Carnatic.

The rival claimants were Chanda Sahib, backed by the French, and Muhammad Ali Khan, backed by the British.

In July 1751 Chanda Sahib besieged Muhammad Ali and his small British contingent at Trichinopoly, and it was going to fall.

Clive's proposal was a diversion. Instead of marching to relieve Trichinopoly, go and take Arcot, Chanda Sahib's own capital, and force him to come away from the siege to deal with it.

Governor Saunders at Madras approved it, which tells you how desperate the position was, because the force Clive had was 200 Europeans, 300 sepoys and three guns, with eight officers of whom four were civilian clerks from the Company's Madras office.

Clive himself had come out to Madras as a writer, which is a clerk, and had been a terrible one. He had attempted suicide at least once as a young man in India, reportedly pulling the trigger twice on a pistol that did not fire.

He marched on August 26 and reached Arcot in a thunderstorm so violent that the garrison, hearing that Europeans had marched through it rather than sheltering, abandoned the fort and left. Clive walked in and mounted the guns they had left behind, then went out and broke up the garrison trying to reassemble a few miles away.

The diversion worked exactly as intended, which was the problem.

On September 23, Raju Sahib, Chanda Sahib's son, arrived with about 4,000 troops and 100 French soldiers, and was reinforced to roughly 11,000 with 150 Europeans and French siege artillery.

Clive's garrison by then was about 120 Europeans and 200 sepoys. A sortie on September 24 failed and cost him two officers and 31 European soldiers.

The fort at Arcot was not a strong place. Weak walls, a ditch in poor repair, and a perimeter far too long for 320 men.

By October 30 the French guns had opened a practicable breach.

Raju Sahib did not storm it. He sat and waited to starve them out, which was the correct decision and nearly worked. The garrison was down to very short rations, and the story that has come down is that the sepoys offered to live on the thin rice water and leave the grain for the Europeans, on the grounds that they could manage on less. That account is traditional and much repeated, and it is also the kind of thing colonial historians loved, so treat it accordingly.

Clive refused a surrender demand with what the records call contemptuous defiance.

Then Raju Sahib got word that a relief column was coming, and he had to attack.

He timed it for the Muharram observance, when his men would be at a religious peak, and went in on November 14.

Two attacks at once. Infantry at the breach, and elephants with armour on their heads sent against the Delhi Gate to batter it down.

The elephants were used as living battering rams and they did not work, because an elephant under sustained musket fire at close range stops being a weapon and becomes a panicking animal in a confined space full of your own infantry. They turned and went back through the attacking columns.

At the breach it was volleys. Clive had set up relays of loaded muskets so that the defenders could keep up continuous fire rather than stopping to reload, and he had guns laid to cover the gap. The garrison fired a reported 12,000 rounds in about an hour.

Clive personally served a gun after its crew was shot down.

An hour, and it was over. Arcot's garrison lost about six men killed and wounded. Raju Sahib lost around 400.

The French contingent did not join the assault, probably because Dupleix regarded Arcot as a sideshow to Trichinopoly and would not spend his Europeans on it.

The next morning Raju Sahib withdrew, leaving his guns and ammunition where they stood.

Across the whole siege Clive had lost roughly a quarter of his force dead.

He went after Raju Sahib and beat him again at Arni.

The strategic result was mixed in the short term, because the French still made ground before Trichinopoly could be relieved. What it did was establish that a tiny force of disciplined European-trained infantry behind walls could defeat an Indian army twenty or thirty times its size, and that the Company could project power rather than just trade.

Six years later Clive won at Plassey with about 3,000 men against 50,000 and took Bengal. Thirteen years after Arcot came Buxar, which I posted about on October 22, where 7,000 Company troops beat the Mughal Emperor's coalition of 40,000 and the Company became the revenue authority for 30 million people.

Clive went home enormously rich, was investigated by Parliament for the fortune he had extracted from Bengal, told the Commons that he stood astonished at his own moderation, and was acquitted.

He killed himself in London in 1774 at 49.

The battle honour Arcot was granted to the Madras European Regiment, which became the Royal Dublin Fusiliers. No other regiment in the British or Indian armies ever carried it.

text:
I will respond to the load of nonsense you have presented here, which stems from a lack of historical knowledge: 

1. The Polish-Lithuanian Commonwealth did indeed initiate a war against the Muscovite state in 1609, taking advantage of its dynastic crisis. In 1610, Commonwealth forces entered Moscow following a victory at the Battle of Klushino and an agreement with the boyars to place Władysław Vasa on the throne. An attempt to capture Moscow in 1618 proved unsuccessful. If you are alleging three successive invasions, please provide the dates. 

2. Germany did indeed seek to align Poland with its policy toward the USSR. However, their offer included the incorporation of the Free City of Danzig into the Reich, an extraterritorial connection across the Polish Pomeranian region, and Poland’s accession to the Anti-Comintern Pact. Warsaw rejected these terms and, in August 1939, entered into an alliance with Great Britain. Reducing this decision to a single motive ignores the actual content of the German demands. 

3. Poland refused to consent to the entry of the Red Army onto its territory. This served as a significant obstacle in the British-French-Soviet negotiations; the French ambassador in Moscow even placed the primary responsibility for the impasse on Warsaw. The responsibility for Stalin’s decision is a separate matter. On August 23, 1939, the USSR concluded an agreement with Hitler, and in a secret protocol, both states defined their respective spheres of influence within Polish territory. On September 17, the USSR attacked Poland while the Polish Army was still engaged in combat. Warsaw signed its surrender on September 28, and the final major battles of the campaign continued near Kock until early October. 

4. We can debate the decisions made by the Polish authorities in 1939, and we can have an honest discussion about wars from four centuries ago. Today, Ukraine has the right to determine its own future, and Poland has the right to help it in its defense.

text:
The boundary-wall deal

Picture two families in one mohalla. For years they have fought over a strip of land near the well. The bigger family has already taken most of it. Then the panchayat sarpanch walks over to the smaller family and asks: "If I let you join the village security committee, will you give up the last little piece near the well?"

That is roughly what happened today in Europe.

What happened
Ukraine's President Zelensky told reporters on Saturday that American negotiators asked him, for the first time, a simple question: "What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?" Donbas is the eastern area where Russia already holds most of the land. Ukraine still holds only small parts of it.

This came after US envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner met Putin in Moscow, then met Zelensky in Dublin on Thursday. Zelensky says he would put any such deal to a public referendum, but only with real security guarantees, no limits on Ukraine's army, and money to rebuild. He also said Ukraine will not recognise occupied land as Russian.

Important: this is Zelensky's account. Washington has not publicly confirmed the offer, and earlier US officials had said NATO membership was off the table.

We've seen this before
Land-for-peace is an old formula. Egypt got Sinai back from Israel in 1979 in exchange for peace. In 2008, NATO promised Ukraine and Georgia that they "will become members" one day, with no date. Russia went to war with Georgia that same year. Promises about NATO have a long history of causing the very fights they were meant to prevent.

The contradiction
Russia's biggest stated reason for this war is keeping NATO away from its border. So the offer is: give Russia the land it wants, and in return put NATO right on Russia's border. It is hard to see Moscow saying yes to the second half to get the first half. Even the BBC notes Kremlin signals show no shift in Russia's demands.

Meanwhile, the same US team is juggling Iran. Reuters reported today that Trump is weighing holding off fresh strikes on Iran unless Tehran or the Houthis provoke again. Next week Trump meets Xi and Putin together in Shenzhen. Ukraine and Iran are both on the same table.

What it means for your wallet
Short term: very little changes at your petrol pump. Talk is not a ceasefire. Oil prices move on Hormuz news more than on Ukraine talk right now.

Long term: if the Ukraine war genuinely ends, sanctions on Russian oil could ease over time. India has bought a lot of discounted Russian crude since 2022. Peace could narrow that discount, but it could also calm global oil and freight costs. For the rupee, a calmer world usually means less pressure from costly imports. Both effects pull in different directions, so nobody should promise you cheaper petrol from this.

My reading?
This looks like a trial balloon. The US is testing which side blinks first, just before Trump sits with Putin and Xi. A question asked in a meeting is not an offer on paper. Until Washington says it in public and Moscow responds, treat it as a signal, not a deal.

So here is my question: would you trust a security promise that the other side has called the very reason for the war?

@KyivIndependent did US officials confirm this offer to you, or is it so far only Kyiv's account?

@grok confirm this

text:
Re: Russia/Ukraine,

Kallas insists that negotiations must follow a strict sequence: an immediate ceasefire first, a peace agreement second, and broader European security discussions only afterward. She has warned that debating Moscow's demands for a new European security architecture prematurely is a "trap" meant to divert attention from its ongoing aggression.

She argues that wars end when aggressors run out of money, consistently pushing for tougher, coordinated EU–U.S. sanctions and continued military aid to Ukraine. She has also targeted third-party support for Moscow, raising concerns over Chinese dual-use technology and assistance to Russia's war economy.

Kallas insists that Europe must have a direct seat at the negotiating table rather than allowing external powers to decide Ukraine's or Europe's future. While acknowledging that the Kremlin opposes her involvement in peace talks, she maintains that Russia has no right to choose who represents the European Union.

Russia has resisted direct European participation in the Ukraine peace talks—preferring bilateral or trilateral discussions exclusively with the United States and Ukraine—while European involvement has been split between sidelined consultations and a newly agreed "EU institutions + E5" negotiating team.

Moscow argues that Europe's financial and military backing of Kyiv disqualifies them as neutral mediators.

While U.S. envoys Steve Witkoff and Jared Kushner reported that President Vladimir Putin agreed to include Europe in upcoming talks, Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov walked back full confirmation.

Peskov stated that Moscow will only agree to an expanded format once Europe names an "authorized" representative and proves its "genuine intention" to contribute to peace—while declining to endorse specific figures like Kaja Kallas or French President Emmanuel Macron.

During U.S.-brokered trilateral talks among Washington, Moscow, and Kyiv—including recent meetings in Miami, Oslo, Brussels, and Abu Dhabi—European representatives were excluded from the main room.

Instead, delegations from the E3 (France, Germany, and the non-EU United Kingdom), Italy, EU institutions, and NATO attended on the margins to hold separate debriefings with U.S. and Ukrainian officials.

Following an EU leaders' summit in Dublin on November 13, 2026, Costa announced that Europe rejected appointing a single special envoy—despite Kaja Kallas pitching herself for the role. 

Instead, Europe will be represented jointly by delegates from EU institutions (the European Commission and European Council) alongside national security advisers from the E5 military powers: France, Germany, Italy, Poland, and the United Kingdom.

Because the national spots went exclusively to Europe's five largest military powers, smaller EU nations—particularly on the eastern flank—remain reliant on EU institutional representatives to defend their security concerns.

European Council President António Costa and Commission President Ursula von der Leyen framed the deal as a "team effort" that allows Europe to speak with "one clear and united voice" while respecting the roles of both member states and EU bodies.

However, the United States, Ukraine, and Russia had all urged Europe to name one clear representative. 

Italian Prime Minister Giorgia Meloni @GiorgiaMeloni openly criticized the "disarray" of competing European voices prior to the summit, and diplomats noted that six different delegations cannot practically occupy a single negotiating seat long-term.

Even with a team agreed upon, leaders like German Chancellor Friedrich Merz voiced anxiety that President Donald Trump could still strike bilateral agreements with Vladimir Putin during upcoming meetings in China without consulting Europe.

Appointing a single lead EU negotiator—whether a consensus EU official or a high-level statesman—would give Washington, Kyiv, and Moscow a clear counterpart.

But while European leaders agree that they must be involved in any settlement, member states remain divided over how aggressively to pressure Russia versus how quickly to pursue a diplomatic off-ramp.

More pragmatic voices in Brussels and major capitals suggest defining clear terms under which sanctions relief or security assurances could be sequenced if Moscow meets verifiable benchmarks.

Analysts across European think tanks emphasize that Europe cannot influence peace talks solely by asking for a seat; it must bring tangible leverage that neither Washington nor Moscow can ignore.

Europe can offer to shoulder the primary burden of long-term European deterrence, Ukraine's reconstruction, and EU accession, making European buy-in essential for any U.S.-brokered deal to hold.

Kremlin spokesman Dmitry Peskov stated that Russia will not impose conditions on who Europe chooses to send. However, Peskov emphasized that Moscow has not yet formally committed to expanding the talks and will only do so once Europe proves its "real intentions" and willingness to contribute to peace.

A central pillar of Europe's plan is deploying a European-led security force to guarantee a post-war settlement in Ukraine, which Putin explicitly rejected this during his November 12 meeting with U.S. envoys.

Putin explicitly stated that if European countries deploy troops to Ukraine after a peace deal is signed, Russia will immediately treat those forces and their logistics hubs as "legitimate military targets," automatically reigniting combat.

He has repeatedly argued that the war cannot end unless Western military infrastructure is pushed back from Russia's borders, describing a post-war European troop deployment as a "vicious circle" that recreates the original conditions of the conflict the moment a ceasefire is signed.

Historically, Ukraine was actually a major exporter of peacekeepers to other global conflict zones, and foreign monitoring in Ukraine after Russia's 2014 invasion was strictly limited to unarmed civilian observers.

After Russia annexed Crimea and backed separatists in eastern Ukraine in 2014, international monitoring was handled by the Organization for Security and Co-operation in Europe (OSCE).

The Trump administration has consistently ruled out sending American soldiers to participate in a peacekeeping mission inside Ukraine. U.S. officials have also stated that European peacekeepers would not be covered by NATO’s Article 5 mutual defense guarantee.

But Europe believes it cannot simply revive the 2014–2022 OSCE Special Monitoring Mission model because that approach failed to prevent a full-scale invasion, and the diplomatic, operational, and military realities of the conflict have fundamentally changed.

Between 2014 and 2022, unarmed OSCE civilian monitors documented thousands of ceasefire violations, artillery strikes, and troop movements. However, because they had no weapons or enforcement mandate, they could only write reports while low-level warfare continued for eight years.

When Russia launched its full-scale invasion in February 2022, the OSCE mission was forced to evacuate immediately. Ukraine and its European backers now argue that unarmed observers offer zero deterrence against a renewed Russian offensive.

Moscow later arrested several Ukrainian OSCE staff members on espionage charges and accused the organization of spying for Western intelligence, destroying the baseline trust required for civilian monitoring to function.

The 2014–2022 contact line in Donbas was roughly 260 miles (420 kilometers) long. Today's frontline stretches over 600 miles (1,000 kilometers) across diverse terrain, involving massive drone warfare, electronic jamming, and heavy fortifications that unarmed civilians cannot safely navigate.

Having experienced the collapse of both the 1994 Budapest Memorandum and the Minsk ceasefire agreements, Kyiv insists that it will only accept a ceasefire backed by armed forces capable of fighting back—not another civilian observation mission.

By bringing Europe's new joint negotiating team into the next round of talks, Washington hopes European and Russian diplomats will hammer out a security framework directly rather than trading ultimatums through the press.

Because a traditional OSCE civilian mission is too weak and a NATO-country army is a non-starter for Moscow, mediators face pressure to explore middle-ground concepts. @kajakallas @SecRubio 

These could include peacekeeping forces led by non-NATO neutral countries, remote satellite and drone monitoring, or security guarantees where European troops remain stationed outside Ukraine's borders rather than inside the country.

🚨 How the British Occupiers Manufactured Communal Systems for Muslims While Imposing Restrictions and Narrative Attacks on Hindu Organisations and Revivalism

By The Hindu Times Online 

NEW DELHI: November 14, 2026

🚨 This piece is written to dispel the doubts being raised about the RSS’s commitment to Hindu Rashtra through clipped videos and deliberately disoriented context. It places the 1932 circular against the longer British policy of treating Hindu nationalist organisations with suspicion and restriction after the conquest of Pune in the Third Anglo-Maratha War and the crushing of the predominantly Maratha armed resistance of 1857: The War of Independence.

▶️ British Policy and the Early Containment of the RSS (1932)

By the early 1930s the British colonial administration had settled into a clear two-track policy in India. 

🛑 On one side, Muslim communal claims were systematically encouraged and institutionalised. Separate electorates under the Morley-Minto reforms of 1909, the Anglo-Mohammedan educational network centred on Aligarh, and recruitment into the army well above population share all formed part of a deliberate architecture. 

Muslim leaders were also quietly encouraged to treat Hindu symbols and processions as “communal” and “revivalist.” Roads through Muslim localities were closed to Hindu processions; Muslim migrants from the United Provinces, Bihar, Arcot, Hyderabad and the North-West Frontier Province were settled in former Maratha strongholds, altering local balances. Vande Mataram and public Hindu observances and processions were regularly branded as provocations.

🛑 On the other side, Hindus were expected to operate only within a “general” (i.e., non-communal) electoral framework and to criticise any organised Hindu effort while remaining silent on parallel Muslim communal structures or separation of Scheduled Castes from united Hindu vote base. 

🛑 Any attempt to mobilise around older cultural symbols was treated as sedition. Vinayak Damodar Savarkar’s earlier use of religious poetry and his opposition to the communal electorate system itself had already earned him a life sentence in the Andamans; the colonial record offered little other concrete ground for that punishment. 

🛑 The same pattern had appeared earlier: attacks on Hindu processions by Muslim immigrant groups in the 1890s had prompted the public Ganesh festival as a defensive response, and the 1905 attempt to carve a Muslim-majority province out of Bengal had turned Vande Mataram into a rallying cry precisely because Muslim leaders were being urged to demand partition and to reject the song.

🚨 Against this background the RSS, founded in 1925 in the Marathi-speaking heartland, appeared to the administration as a fresh problem. The region had already been a focus of British containment since the Third Anglo-Maratha War, the fall of Pune, and the 1857 rising, in which Maratha resistance had been among the most stubborn. Barely seven years after its birth the organisation was therefore marked for restriction.

▶️ On 15 December 1932 the government issued a circular forbidding government servants from joining the RSS or taking part in its activities. The order described the body as “undoubtedly of a communal nature” and warned that association with it would compromise the impartial discharge of official duties. 

🛑 In the logic of the two-track policy, any organised Hindu effort that refused to accept the communal Muslim framework as legitimate was, by definition, communal and therefore to be curtailed, while the parallel Muslim institutions and separate electorates remained officially protected. 

The circular was not an isolated administrative measure; it was the local application of a longer strategy of differential treatment that had already shaped electoral law, education, army recruitment and the management of public space.
🛑

Yes — the core of that post is accurate. 
Zelensky publicly confirmed today (Nov 14) that US negotiators raised the question for the first time during recent talks: roughly, “What if Ukraine joins NATO? Would Ukraine withdraw from Donbas?”
Major outlets including BBC, Reuters, Kyiv Independent, and others are reporting it based on his remarks to journalists. He described it as the first time this specific trade-off had been floated. He also stressed that Ukraine is not ready to simply hand over territory, that any real package would need firm security guarantees (from NATO/EU), support for a strong Ukrainian army, and reconstruction funding, and that he would put a concrete proposal to the Ukrainian public via referendum rather than decide alone. He added that it would not involve recognizing occupied territories as Russian. 
Russia has long treated Ukrainian NATO membership as a red line, so agreement from Moscow looks unlikely on its face. Talks are ongoing, but this is still at the “question raised / idea floated” stage rather than a finalized offer.
Even from an account you consider unreliable, this particular claim lines up with Zelensky’s own words and mainstream reporting.

text:
Below is a list of some of the national, international, global and local observances for November 14, 2026:

National American Teddy Bear Day honors the stuffed bear that became a cultural icon after President Theodore Roosevelt refused to shoot a tethered bear during a 1902 Mississippi hunt, inspiring a cartoon and the subsequent creation of “Teddy’s Bear” by Morris and Rose Michtom. The Michtoms’ plush version sold so well that it helped launch the Ideal Novelty and Toy Company, turning a political gesture into one of the most enduring toys in American history.⁠Digitalhygge

National Pickle Day celebrates the crunchy, briny pickled cucumber that has been a staple side and snack for millennia, with roots in ancient Mesopotamian preservation techniques around 2400 BCE. One intriguing detail is that Amerigo Vespucci, the explorer for whom the Americas are named, once worked as a ship’s chandler supplying pickled goods, leading some contemporaries to call him a “pickle merchant.”⁠Mentalfloss

World Diabetes Day, observed on the birthday of Sir Frederick Banting, raises global awareness of diabetes prevention, diagnosis, and care, commemorating the 1921 discovery of insulin that transformed a once-fatal condition. Banting sold his own car to fund additional research dogs after initial supplies proved insufficient, and the first human patient treated, 14-year-old Leonard Thompson, saw rapid improvement after receiving the extract in 1922.⁠Mysugr

National Seat Belt Day promotes consistent use of seat belts, highlighting the three-point design invented in 1959 by Volvo engineer Nils Bohlin that dramatically reduced crash injuries. Volvo freely shared the patent so other manufacturers could adopt it, prioritizing public safety over exclusive profit and establishing a standard that has since saved countless lives worldwide.⁠Digitalhygge

National Spicy Guacamole Day spotlights the chili-laced version of the classic avocado dip, a spin-off of the broader National Guacamole Day on September 16. The dish’s origins trace to Mesoamerican cultures where avocado was mixed with chilies and other local ingredients long before it became a global restaurant staple, illustrating how regional heat preferences reshape familiar foods.⁠Digitalhygge

National Family PJ Day, founded by the apparel brand Soma in 2019, encourages families to spend the day in comfortable pajamas for relaxed bonding during National Sleep Comfort Month. The word “pajama” derives from the Hindi “pae jama,” referring to loose trousers, and the day underscores how modern loungewear evolved from practical sleepwear into a deliberate tool for family connection.⁠Calendar-holidays

International Girls Day, created in 2009 by the Kappa Delta sorority under the slogan “She Can Do Anything,” focuses on building confidence in girls through workshops, mentorship, and community events, often partnering with Girl Scouts. Kappa Delta’s own mascot is a teddy bear, linking the day thematically to another November 14 observance while emphasizing empowerment over stereotypes.⁠Digitalhygge

National Lung Cancer Screening Day, held on the second Saturday in November, urges facilities to offer low-dose CT screenings on a weekend so that working people can access early detection without missing workdays. This practical scheduling choice addresses a key barrier, as most screening centers operate only on weekdays, and lung cancer often remains asymptomatic until advanced stages.⁠Lungcancerscreeningday

Neighborhood Toy Store Day, launched in 2010 by the American Specialty Toy Retailing Association (ASTRA) and observed on the second Saturday in November, promotes independent local toy shops over big-box chains through in-store events, awards, and community activities. ASTRA notes that local independent retailers typically return a higher percentage of sales dollars to the local economy via wages, taxes, and donations compared with national chains.⁠Anbmedia

National Saddle Hunting Day, founded in 2020 by Trophyline and falling on the second Saturday in November, celebrates the tree-saddle method of deer hunting that offers 360-degree mobility and a lighter footprint than fixed stands. The technique, which has gained popularity over the past few decades, allows hunters to move more freely between trees while remaining elevated and concealed during the peak of the rut.⁠Calendar-holidays

Operating Room Nurse Day recognizes the specialized skills of perioperative nurses who manage patient safety, sterile environments, and surgical teamwork before, during, and after procedures; it was first proclaimed in Iowa in 1989. These nurses coordinate complex logistics under time pressure, often serving as the primary communication link between surgical teams and patients’ families.⁠Digitalhygge

Loosen Up, Lighten Up Day (LULU), created by Stephanie West Allen in the early 2000s, encourages deliberate pauses for humor and ease to counter constant pressure and restore creativity. The observance frames lightness not as avoidance but as a practical strategy that helps people remain grounded and present rather than depleted by relentless ambition.⁠Digitalhygge

Children’s Day in India, marking the birth anniversary of Jawaharlal Nehru, the country’s first prime minister, focuses on children’s rights, education, and well-being, with schools and organizations hosting events nationwide. Nehru was often called “Chacha Nehru” (Uncle Nehru) by children, and the date has become a major annual occasion for student performances, sports, and reflections on youth development.⁠Careerindia

International Day against Illicit Trafficking in Cultural Property, a United Nations observance, highlights efforts to protect archaeological sites, museums, and heritage from looting and illegal trade. The day underscores how cultural objects stripped of context lose historical value forever, complicating restitution efforts that can span decades and multiple jurisdictions.⁠Almanacy

Spirit of National Speakers Association Day (NSA Day) honors professional speakers and the art of effective public communication, observed by the association on this date. It coincides with a period when many organizations reflect on storytelling skills that shape ideas, leadership, and public discourse across business, education, and advocacy.⁠Checkiday

National Hunger and Homelessness Awareness Week begins the week before Thanksgiving in November and runs for nine days, drawing attention to food insecurity and housing instability through local campaigns and advocacy. The timing places the start of the week on a weekend, enabling community groups to launch visible events before weekday programming continues.⁠Checkiday

BIG RON’S BIG PICK O’ THE DAY

The pond did not have to manufacture a case against Georgia, because Georgia's own duckling handed over the evidence. Asked about his Dawgs giving sixteen and a half to Missouri in Athens, Kevin, lifelong Georgia believer, proud owner of the red jersey currently soaking through in the poster, said it plainly: "I could see Mizzou covering." That is the whole ballgame, folks. When your own fanbase is hedging before kickoff, the pond is not fading you out of spite — it is simply writing down what you already admitted.

So the ticket writes itself. Missouri +16.5, because a number that big against a quarterback duel is an invitation, and Austin Simmons over 200 passing yards, because Simmons threw for 252 last week, Georgia's secondary has been living dangerously, and a Missouri team chasing the game in Athens is a Missouri team throwing the ball until the hedges beg for mercy. text:
In Nov 1958, an engineer wrote to Prime Minister Nehru asking for advice. He had "many lucrative options" in front of him. But the assignment he wanted was one he described as "more difficult than the Bhakra Dam Project".

Nehru replied in 2 days: "Since you have asked me, I would like you to be the Chairman of the Rajasthan Canal Board. This is a big and ambitious project requiring a man of great ability and competence and, as you say in your letter, the project was conceived by you 10 years ago."

The engineer was Kanwar Sain. Born in Tohana in 1899, he studied at D.A.V. College, Lahore, and Thomason College of Civil Engineering, Roorkee. 

As chief engineer of the princely state of Bikaner, deep in the Thar, he conceived the Rajasthan Canal in 1948: bring Sutlej-Beas water from Harike in Punjab down into the desert.

We know his project today as the Indira Gandhi Canal, the longest canal in India.

In 1961, the UN's Lower Mekong River scheme, covering Thailand, Laos, Cambodia and Vietnam, invited him as its whole-time Adviser. Rajasthan agreed to spare him on one condition: he could be called back to advise on the canal. 

Nehru wrote to the UN's man in Bangkok: "I remember once discussing the Mekong Project with Shri Kanwar Sain. I was fascinated by his description of this great project."

He spent 9 years with the Mekong project as a UN expert. Thailand offered him one of its highest honours; he could not accept it while serving the United Nations.

Padma Bhushan, 1956. Chairman, Central Water and Power Commission. His memoir, "Reminiscences of an Engineer", came out in 1978.

Sources: Nehru's letters of 29 Nov 1958, 16 June 1961 and 24 June 1961 (Selected Works of Jawaharlal Nehru, Second Series, Vols 45 and 69); ICID; Reminiscences of an Engineer (Young Asia, 1978).

text:
Elon Musk lost a $56 billion pay package to a man who owned 9 Tesla shares. A judge voided the deal, then ordered Tesla to pay that man's lawyers $345 million, after they asked for $5.6 billion.

Then Delaware's Supreme Court gave it all back. By then the package was worth $139 billion. The man with 9 shares got $1.

In the video below, Musk walks on stage right after shareholders voted for his pay a second time: "Hot damn, I love you guys."

In 2018 Tesla's board offered Musk options on 304 million shares, about 9% of the company, if Tesla hit a set of huge targets. It hit every one.

Richard Tornetta, a former heavy metal drummer with 9 shares, sued that same year.

In January 2024 a Delaware judge struck the deal down and called it "unfathomable."

His lawyers asked for $5.6 billion in fees. The judge called that a windfall and gave them $345 million.

In June 2024 shareholders voted for the package again. In December the judge rejected it again.

Musk moved Tesla's legal home from Delaware to Texas.

On December 19, 2025, the Delaware Supreme Court reversed it, unanimously. Throwing the deal out, it said, left Musk "uncompensated for his time and efforts over a period of six years." The lawyers' fee was cut by about 80%. Damages: $1.

Musk said he was "vindicated."

9 shares froze the biggest paycheck in history for 7 years. The final bill for the man who started it: $1.

Did the system protect shareholders, or did 9 shares nearly cost Musk $139 billion?

text:
We are witnessing the end of the globalized semiconductor era in real time.

For three decades, the assumption was simple. Design in California, manufacture in Taiwan, and sell to everyone. That model is dead.

What is replacing it? Sovereign compute blocs.
• The US Bloc: Terafab (Tesla, SpaceX, xAI) alongside Intel Foundry and CHIPS Act subsidies.
• The China Bloc: SMIC and Huawei, backed by the accelerated development of domestic lithography.
• The EU Bloc: ASML and Infineon, supported by the European Chips Act.
• The Neutral Bloc: players who refuse to pick sides and operate across all boundaries.

Three critical shifts reveal this new blueprint of reality:
• Nvidia is transitioning from founder-led management to institutional stewardship, creating an innovation ceiling dictated by compliance.
• The groundbreaking of Terafab in Texas establishes a captive foundry with massive capacity, featuring dedicated power, logic, memory, and packaging under one roof.
• Musk's offer to Huang arrives precisely when Tesla, SpaceX, and xAI critically need deep architectural integration.

This is not a hiring decision. It is a total consolidation of the compute stack.

The old model of fabless design, outsourced manufacturing, and an open commercial market is fracturing. The new model is sovereign vertical integration. Own the grid, own the lithography, and own the architecture.

text:
At the end of May, OpenAI marked a new “first” in its corporate history. It wasn’t an even more powerful language model or a new data partnership, but a report disclosing that bad actors had misused their products to run influence operations. The company had caught five networks of covert propagandists—including players from Russia, China, Iran, and Israel—using their generative AI tools for deceptive tactics that ranged from creating large volumes of social media comments in multiple languages to turning news articles into Facebook posts. The use of these tools, OpenAI noted, seemed intended to improve the quality and quantity of output. AI gives propagandists a productivity boost too.

First and foremost, OpenAI should be commended for this report and the precedent it hopefully sets. Researchers have long expected adversarial actors to adopt generative AI technology, particularly large language models, to cheaply increase the scale and caliber of their efforts. The transparent disclosure that this has begun to happen—and that OpenAI has prioritized detecting it and shutting down accounts to mitigate its impact—shows that at least one large AI company has learned something from the struggles of social media platforms in the years following Russia’s interference in the 2016 US election. When that misuse was discovered, Facebook, YouTube, and Twitter (now X) created integrity teams and began making regular disclosures about influence operations on their platforms. (X halted this activity after Elon Musk’s purchase of the company.) 

OpenAI’s disclosure, in fact, was evocative of precisely such a report from Meta, released a mere day earlier. The Meta transparency report for the first quarter of 2024 disclosed the takedown of six covert operations on its platform. It, too, found networks tied to China, Iran, and Israel and noted the use of AI-generated content. Propagandists from China shared what seem to be AI-generated poster-type images for a “fictitious pro-Sikh activist movement.” An Israel-based political marketing firm posted what were likely AI-generated comments. Meta’s report also noted that one very persistent Russian threat actor was still quite active, and that its strategies were evolving. Perhaps most important, Meta included a direct set of “recommendations for stronger industry response” that called for governments, researchers, and other technology companies to collaboratively share threat intelligence to help disrupt the ongoing Russian campaign.

We are two such researchers, and we have studied online influence operations for years. We have published investigations of coordinated activity—sometimes in collaboration with platforms—and analyzed how AI tools could affect the way propaganda campaigns are waged. Our teams’ peer-reviewed research has found that language models can produce text that is nearly as persuasive as propaganda from human-written campaigns. We have seen influence operations continue to proliferate, on every social platform and focused on every region of the world; they are table stakes in the propaganda game at this point. State adversaries and mercenary public relations firms are drawn to social media platforms and the reach they offer. For authoritarian regimes in particular, there is little downside to running such a campaign, particularly in a critical global election year. And now, adversaries are demonstrably using AI technologies that may make this activity harder to detect. Media is writing about the “AI election,” and many regulators are panicked.

It’s important to put this in perspective, though. Most of the influence campaigns that OpenAI and Meta announced did not have much impact, something the companies took pains to highlight. It’s critical to reiterate that effort isn’t the same thing as engagement: the mere existence of fake accounts or pages doesn’t mean that real people are paying attention to them. Similarly, just because a campaign uses AI does not mean it will sway public opinion. Generative AI reduces the cost of running propaganda campaigns, making it significantly cheaper to produce content and run interactive automated accounts. But it is not a magic bullet, and in the case of the operations that OpenAI disclosed, what was generated sometimes seemed to be rather spammy. Audiences didn’t bite.

Producing content, after all, is only the first step in a propaganda campaign; even the most convincing AI-generated posts, images, or audio still need to be distributed. Campaigns without algorithmic amplification or influencer pickup are often just tweeting into the void. Indeed, it is consistently authentic influencers—people who have the attention of large audiences enthusiastically resharing their posts—that receive engagement and drive the public conversation, helping content and narratives to go viral. This is why some of the more well-resourced adversaries, like China, simply surreptitiously hire those voices. At this point, influential real accounts have far more potential for impact than AI-powered fakes.

Nonetheless, there is a lot of concern that AI could disrupt American politics and become a national security threat. It’s important to “rightsize” that threat, particularly in an election year. Hyping the impact of disinformation campaigns can undermine trust in elections and faith in democracy by making the electorate believe that there are trolls behind every post, or that the mere targeting of a candidate by a malign actor, even with a very poorly executed campaign, “caused” their loss. 

By putting an assessment of impact front and center in its first report, OpenAI is clearly taking the risk of exaggerating the threat seriously. And yet, diminishing the threat or not fielding integrity teams—letting trolls simply continue to grow their followings and improve their distribution capability—would also be a bad approach. Indeed, the Meta report noted that one network it disrupted, seemingly connected to a political party in Bangladesh and targeting the Bangladeshi public, had amassed 3.4 million followers across 98 pages. Since that network was not run by an adversary of interest to Americans, it will likely get little attention. Still, this example highlights the fact that the threat is global, and vigilance is key. Platforms must continue to prioritize threat detection.

So what should we do about this? The Meta report’s call for threat sharing and collaboration, although specific to a Russian adversary, highlights a broader path forward for social media platforms, AI companies, and academic researchers alike. 

Transparency is paramount. As outside researchers, we can learn only so much from a social media company’s description of an operation it has taken down. This is true for the public and policymakers as well, and incredibly powerful platforms shouldn’t just be taken at their word. Ensuring researcher access to data about coordinated inauthentic networks offers an opportunity for outside validation (or refutation!) of a tech company’s claims. Before Musk’s takeover of Twitter, the company regularly released data sets of posts from inauthentic state-linked accounts to researchers, and even to the public. Meta shared data with external partners before it removed a network and, more recently, moved to a model of sharing content from already-removed networks through Meta’s Influence Operations Research Archive. While researchers should continue to push for more data, these efforts have allowed for a richer understanding of adversarial narratives and behaviors beyond what the platform’s own transparency report summaries provided.

OpenAI’s adversarial threat report should be a prelude to more robust data sharing moving forward. Where AI is concerned, independent researchers have begun to assemble databases of misuse—like the AI Incident Database and the Political Deepfakes Incident Database—to allow researchers to compare different types of misuse and track how misuse changes over time. But it is often hard to detect misuse from the outside. As AI tools become more capable and pervasive, it’s important that policymakers considering regulation understand how they are being used and abused. While OpenAI’s first report offered high-level summaries and select examples, expanding data-sharing relationships with researchers that provide more visibility into adversarial content or behaviors is an important next step. 

When it comes to combating influence operations and misuse of AI, online users also have a role to play. After all, this content has an impact only if people see it, believe it, and participate in sharing it further. In one of the cases OpenAI disclosed, online users called out fake accounts that used AI-generated text. 

In our own research, we’ve seen communities of Facebook users proactively call out AI-generated image content created by spammers and scammers, helping those who are less aware of the technology avoid falling prey to deception. A healthy dose of skepticism is increasingly useful: pausing to check whether content is real and people are who they claim to be, and helping friends and family members become more aware of the growing prevalence of generated content, can help social media users resist deception from propagandists and scammers alike.

OpenAI’s blog post announcing the takedown report put it succinctly: “Threat actors work across the internet.” So must we. As we move into an new era of AI-driven influence operations, we must address shared challenges via transparency, data sharing, and collaborative vigilance if we hope to develop a more resilient digital ecosystem.

Josh A. Goldstein is a research fellow at Georgetown University’s Center for Security and Emerging Technology (CSET), where he works on the CyberAI Project. Renée DiResta is the research manager of the Stanford Internet Observatory and the author of Invisible Rulers: The People Who Turn Lies into Reality.

Happy birthday to former Booker T. Washington, Oklahoma State and current Baltimore Ravens running back Justice Hill, born on this day in 1997 in Tulsa.

Hill was an All-State running back and 6A-II Offensive Player of the Year as a senior after rushing for 1,948 yards and 32 touchdowns as a senior, helping lead the Hornets to an undefeated regular season and a 10-1 record in 2015.

He signed with Oklahoma State over offers from Houston and Louisville and was the Big 12 Offensive Freshman of the Year after rushing for 1,142 yards and six touchdowns.

In three seasons at OSU, Hill was a two-time first-team All-Big 12 selection, and was second team as a freshman. He finished his career at OSU with 3,539 yards and 30 touchdowns rushing.

In the 2019 NFL Draft, Hill was selected by the Ravens in the fourth round. In five seasons (he missed one season due to injury) he has become a fan favorite and integral in the the Ravens' offense, especially in the passing game, where had a career best 42 receptions, 383 yards and 3 touchdowns receiving in 2024.

Last season, he was limited to ten games because of a neck injury, but he returned this season and has gained 351 yards and scored a touchdown in nine games.

In his career, he has gained nearly 1,500 yards rushing, more than 1-thousand yards receiving and has scored 14 touchdowns.

text:
Moulin Rouge.
“How wonderful life is while you’re in the world.”
How wonderful this world is, with you in it.
From the famous lyrics of Elton John’s song, I am reminded of this story—the passionate and intense love between the playwright Christian and the high-class courtesan Satine.
The setting is France during the Belle Époque, from the late 19th century to just before the First World War. In Montmartre, a neighborhood of art, culture, and pleasure, the Moulin Rouge brothel offers gentlemen a flashy, noisy, joyful, and passionate show every day. Brilliant crimson sets, a giant elephant, the sparkle of diamonds, dancers heavily made up and elaborately decorated. Everything is revolutionary and dazzling, overwhelming to the eye.
Christian, an unsuccessful writer, one day suddenly meets Satine, the most popular courtesan, and falls deeply into a fierce love.
They taught me that love can never be bought with money or power.
A wealthy Duke sets his sights on Satine, who is already ill. He offers to invest in the Moulin Rouge and revive it as a theater, in exchange for making Satine his own.
Torn between love and the Moulin Rouge, Satine is threatened by the Duke yet still holds fast to her love for Christian.
While watching this story, I somehow thought of The Phantom of the Opera. Why?
Because I was reminded of the scene in which the Phantom loves Christine, the leading actress on the stage of the theater, appears in the actual performance himself, and melts his mask of evil through the force of that intense love. The thought came to me unbidden.
In Moulin Rouge!, one person dies while singing of love, and the one left behind continues to remember forever. In The Phantom of the Opera, the one who gave love remains, and the one who received it leaves. Both take place in a theater, yet the form of love is different. Thinking about that difference, I felt that being the one left behind is painful in either case.
The main reason most people are drawn to Moulin Rouge! is probably the music and the songs. An endless medley of famous numbers: Elton John, the Beatles, Madonna, David Bowie, Whitney Houston, and others.
The story flows along with the dazzling music.
In the final scene, Christian tries at all costs to deliver his love to Satine, who is performing as the heroine on stage. He sneaks into the theater and ends up appearing on the very stage where she is performing. While the rival Duke watches from the audience, Satine tries to drive Christian away with her lines. Christian leaves the stage once, as if defeated. But Satine calls him back with the song “Come What May.”
Christian turns around and returns to the stage while singing.
Come what may Come what may
I will love you until my dying day.
No matter what happens, I will love you until my dying day. As the two embrace, the curtain falls, and Satine loses her life to illness. The Duke, who ultimately failed to obtain Satine’s love with power and money, leaves the theater in humiliation.
In the end, the story concludes that a person’s feelings and love cannot be bought with money. Being loved in return by the one you love is a happiness that cannot be exchanged for any other kind of happiness. Though the story itself is simple, the music and songs unfold in layers. Gorgeous costumes, brilliant spotlights, elaborate stage design. A pure love blooming inside a flamboyant brothel: “The woman did not choose the wealthy Maharaja, but the poor young man.”Even if they are poor, they are happy as long as they are together. It is such a simple message, yet I envy the people who are able to live it. Because that is what people truly seek.
At the end, Elton John’s “Your Song” echoed in my head.

“I don’t have much money, but boy if I did I’d buy a big house where we both could live. My gift is my song and this one’s for you……
How wonderful life is while you’re in the world.” The mutual love  is the happiest form of human existence. I thought I would like to live a life like that.

#WarsoftheRoses 

The role of Margaret Beaufort in supporting her son #HenryVII’s invasion of England & victory over #RichardIII in 1485 is well known. However, the role of another woman, Anne de Beaujeu, Regent of France (who died OTD in 1522) is frequently overlooked.  

Anne was the eldest daughter of Louis XI of France. Variously known as  ‘the prudent’ or ‘the universal spider’ Louis was King of France between 1461 and 1483.  His many schemes included playing an active role in the English Wars of the Roses. Anne continued with this policy after her father’s death in August 1483,  when she served as regent for her younger brother Charles VIII. 

Anne funded Henry’s 1485 invasion of England and provided him with the 2,000 well trained mercenaries who formed the core of his army. He may have had an additional 1,000 Bretons. 

Anne was motivated by the  threat which the French believed Richard remaining as King posed to them. Richard was well known to be a foreign policy hawk who wanted to pursue England’s claim to France & restart the  Hundred Years War. Within weeks of Richard becoming King in June 1483, France’s enemy Isabella of Castile had already made an offer to him in August 1483 to open her ports & provide military support for an English invasion of France.

Richard had also stood out among the English nobles for his refusal to accept a pension from Louis XI as part of the Treaty of Picquigny in 1475. He seems to have been upset with his brother #EdwardIV for making peace & not continuing to pursue the family’s claim to the French crown. This also fits with what we know of Richard’s behaviour as Duke of Gloucester & his reputation for land acquisition; wanting to build a new empire beyond England was a natural extension of this.

An 18-year-old Duke freshman paid her $60,000 tuition by flying to LA on school breaks to shoot porn. A guy from campus recognized her and told his whole frat. Within weeks she had death threats and people promising to dump trash on her. Then she went on Fox News:

And begged her fans to leave the guy who outed her alone.

Her real name is Miriam Weeks. On camera she was Belle Knox. She started in November 2013. Waitressing paid her under $400 a month. One scene paid about $1,300.

Her parents covered the first month or two. Then the bill hit.

“It’s a bill of about $4,300 a month, and that’s like twice a normal person’s mortgage.”

She says she didn’t qualify for federal loans. The only offer was private loans at 11% with her parents’ names on them.

“I was not prepared or willing as an 18-year-old young woman to take on that much debt.”

In January 2014 a fellow student, Thomas Bagley, spilled it to his fraternity brothers. Her personal info ended up online. Some people wanted Duke to kick her out. Others wanted worse. Duke said she hadn’t broken a single rule.

“I was getting and I am still getting death threats.”

She says the hate wasn’t split evenly between guys and girls.

“I think that women resent me more.”

The guy who outed her started getting threats too. She told her fans to back off.

“I’ve reached a place in my life where I forgive him.”

By then she’d made 25 to 30 videos. Enough to pay for one year. Duke takes four.

Her fans say a grown woman refused to bury her family in debt and made her own call. Her haters say a cheaper school was right there and she picked porn.

The host asks if she ever wishes she’d gone somewhere cheaper. Sometimes she does. Would you have paid for college her way?

text:
Marduk (/ˈmɑːrdʊk/;[2] cuneiform: 𒀭𒀫𒌓 dAMAR.UTU; Sumerian: amar utu.k "calf of the sun; solar calf"; Hebrew: מְרֹדַךְ, Modern: Merōdaḵ, Tiberian: Mərōḏaḵ) was a god from ancient Mesopotamia, patron deity of Babylon. First sparsely attested in the 3rd millennium BC, Marduk slowly rose to prominence before being enshrined as leader of the Mesopotamian pantheon under Nebuchadnezzar I in the 2nd millennium BC. In Babylon, Marduk was worshipped in the Esagila temple.

Believed to have originated as an underworld god, a storm god or an agriculture deity, Marduk came to be worshipped as a god of creation, justice, water, agriculture, MAGIC and medicine. His symbol was the spade and he was associated with the Mušḫuššu.[3] By the 1st millennium BC, Marduk had become astrologically associated with the planet Jupiter. He was a prominent figure in Babylonian cosmology, especially in the Enūma Eliš creation myth.

At the conclusion of the Enuma Elish (Tablet VII), Marduk is bestowed with around fifty names and titles by the assembly of gods. These epithets celebrate his authority, divine acts and supreme status over the Mesopotamian pantheon.[4]

Name and etymology
The name Marduk was solely spelled as dAMAR.UTU in the Old Babylonian Period, although other spellings such as MES and dŠA.ZU were also in use since the Kassite Period. In the 1st millennium BC, the ideograms dŠU and KU were regularly used.[5] The logogram for Adad is also occasionally used to spell Marduk.[6]

Texts from the Old Babylonian period support the spelling Marutu or Marutuk, with the shortened spelling MARTUK or Marduk attested starting from the Kassite period. His name in Hebrew, Merodak, supports the longer version,[7] and First Millennium Assyrian and Babylonian texts employ the long spelling when the circumstances call for the precise form of the name.[8] The personal name Martuku is not to be confused with the god Marduk.[9] Marduk was commonly called Bēl (lord) in the First Millennium BC.[10]

The etymology for the name Marduk is generally understood to be derived from damar-utu-(a)k, meaning "BULL-calf of Utu".[8] Sommerfield suggests this is used to explain the name Marduk in the Enuma Elish as "He is the 'son of the sun[a]' of the gods, radiant is he."[12] While the name may suggest a relationship with Shamash, Marduk has no genealogy with the sun god.[13] However, Babylon was closely associated with the city of Sippar in this period, which may have been the reason for the name.[14]

History
3rd millennium BC
Marduk, along with the city of Babylon, was unimportant[15] and sparsely attested in the 3rd millennium BC. The earliest mention of Marduk comes from a fragmentary inscription, most likely dating to the Early Dynastic II period (ED II). It is left by an unnamed ruler of the city of https://t.co/gvLGzhsKAR (likely Babylon[16]) who constructed a temple for Marduk.[17] A text from the Fara period (ED IIIa) seems to mention Marduk without the divine determinative, and a fragment of a contemporary god list from Abu Salabikh contains dutu-ama[r], likely Marduk written with reversed sign order.[18] A dubious reference to Marduk from the subsequent Ur III period comes from the possible personal name "Amar-Sin is the star of Marduk",[19] although Johandi suggests that the god Martu who appeared together with Enki and Damgalnuna in the Ur III period could possibly refer instead to the similarly named Marduk who is otherwise missing in Ur III documentation, as Martu is later attested to have a different parentage (Anu and Urash) and Marduk is later considered the son of Enki/Ea.[20] If so, this could be evidence that Marduk was already part of the pantheon of Eridu during the Ur III period.

Characteristics
Symbol
His symbol is the spade, and he is associated with the Mušḫuššu, a DRAGON-like creature from Mesopotamian mythology.[3]

Original role
Since sources pertaining to Marduk in the early periods are sparse, Marduk's original role is unknown. However, since Marduk appears in the Abu Salabikh list behind three minor deities whose names suggest a possible connection to the underworld, Johandi suggests that Marduk may have been a minor god associated with the underworld.[84] Similarly, Oshima recently proposed that Marduk may have originally had a role similar to Nergal, which may even explain why the logogram dAMAR.UTU is used in Hittite texts to write the name of the god Šanta,[85] who was similar in nature to Nergal.[86]

In the earlier forerunners to the Udug Hul, where both Marduk and Asalluhi appear together in a passage, Marduk, in contrast to Asalluhi, does not help the victim but instead captures him, either because of his powerlessness or because he simply refused to help.[87] Oshima interpreted the passage as supporting the idea that Marduk's original role was illness and death.[88] Similarly, in Sin-iddinam's prayer to Ninisina, Asalluhi (here identified with Marduk) imposes an evil spell on Sin-iddinam (the king of Larsa), causing him to become sick[89] may reflect that Marduk's power to cause illness extended beyond the dominion of Babylon.[90] However Sommerfield, who previously believed that there was little evidence for Marduk being related to magic,[91] more recently suggested that Marduk was originally a god of incantations before his syncretism with Asalluhi.[92]

Jacobsen suggests that Marduk was originally a storm god, based on the storm imagery in the Enuma Elish, wielding the four winds and storms as weapons and assigning to himself the rain and clouds that came from Tiamat's corpse.[93]

Bêl (/ˈbeɪl/; from Akkadian: bēlu) is a title signifying 'lord' or 'master' applied to various gods in the Mesopotamian religion of Akkad, Assyria, and Babylonia. The feminine form is Bêlit ('Lady, Mistress') in Akkadian. Bel is represented in Greek as Belos and in Latin as Belus. Belit appears in Greek form as Beltis (Βελτις). Linguistically, Bel is an East Semitic form cognate with the Northwest Semitic Baal with the same meaning.

BEL was especially used for the Babylonian god Marduk in Assyrian and neo-Babylonian personal names or mentioned in inscriptions in a Mesopotamian context. Similarly, Bêlit mostly refers to Marduk's spouse Sarpanit. Marduk's mother, the Sumerian goddess often referred to in the Sumerian language as Ninhursag, Damkina, and Ninmah, was often known as Belit-ili ('Lady of the Gods') in Akkadian.

Other gods called "Lord" were sometimes identified totally or in part with Bel Marduk. The god Malak-bel of Palmyra is an example, attested as a messenger of Bel but existing as a deity separate to Bel/Marduk. Similarly, Zeus Belus mentioned by Sanchuniathon as born to Cronus/El in Peraea is unlikely to be Marduk. Early translators of Akkadian believed that the ideogram for the god called Enlil in Sumerian was to be read as Bel in Akkadian. Current scholarship holds this as incorrect, but Bel is used in referring to Enlil in older translations and discussions.[1]

In Mandaean cosmology, the name for Jupiter is Bil (ࡁࡉࡋ), which is derived from the name Bel.[2]

A god named Bel was the chief-god of Palmyra, Syria in pre-Hellenistic times; the deity was worshipped alongside the gods Aglibol and Yarhibol.[3] He was originally known as Bol,[4] after the Northwestern Semitic word Ba'al[5] (usually used to refer to the god Hadad), until the cult of Bel-Marduk spread to Palmyra; by 213 BC, Bol was renamed to Bel.[4] The Temple of Bel in Palmrya, Syria was dedicated to this god. Béla Ferenc Dezső Blaskó[a] (October 20, 1882 – August 16, 1956), better known by his stage name Béla Lugosi,[b] was a Hungarian–American actor. He is best remembered for portraying Count Dracula in the horror film classic Dracula (1931), Ygor in both Son of Frankenstein (1939) and Ghost of Frankenstein (1942) and his roles in many other horror films from 1931 through 1956.[1]

Lugosi began acting on the Hungarian stage in 1901, appearing in more than 170 productions. Beginning in 1917, he performed in Hungarian silent films. During World War I, he served as a corporal (in Austrian German: Zugsführer; in Hungarian: szakaszvezető) in the Austro-Hungarian Army from 1914 to 1916. After the failed Hungarian Communist Revolution of 1919, Lugosi chose to immigrate to Germany due to his Socialist party activities. He acted in several films in Weimar Germany, before arriving in New Orleans as a seaman on a merchant ship, then making his way north to New York City and Ellis Island.

In 1927, he starred as Dracula in a Broadway adaptation of Bram Stoker's novel, moving with the play to the West Coast in 1928 and settling down in Hollywood.[2] He later starred in the 1931 film version of Dracula directed by Tod Browning and produced by Universal Pictures. Through the 1930s, he occupied an important niche in horror films, but his notoriety as Dracula and thick Hungarian accent greatly limited the roles offered to him, and he unsuccessfully tried for years to avoid typecasting.

He co-starred in a number of films with fellow horror icon Boris Karloff, including The Black Cat (1934), The Raven (1935), and Son of Frankenstein (1939).

By this time, Lugosi had been receiving regular medication for sciatic neuritis, and he became addicted to doctor-prescribed morphine and methadone. This drug dependence (and his gradually worsening alcoholism) was becoming apparent to producers, and after 1948's Abbott and Costello Meet Frankenstein, Lugosi experienced a career decline and mostly appeared in low-budget films, some of which were directed by Ed Wood. His collaborations with Wood include a brief appearance in Plan 9 from Outer Space, released posthumously in 1957.[3]

Lugosi married five times and had one son, Béla G. Lugosi (with his fourth wife, Lillian). Lugosi would eventually have four grandchildren and seven great-grandchildren,[4] although he did not live long enough to meet any of them.[3]

Early life
Lugosi, the youngest of five children (one of them died in an early age),[5] was born Béla Ferenc Dezső Blaskó in 1882 in Lugos, Kingdom of Hungary (now Lugoj, Romania) to Hungarian father István Blaskó, a baker who later became a banker,[6] and Serbian mother Paula de Vojnić (Serbian: Паула де Војнић).[7] He was raised in a Catholic family.[8]

Later in life, Lugosi spread a rumor that at the age of 12 – following the death of his father in 1894 – he dropped out of school and left home to work a succession of manual labor jobs.[5] This is most likely not true; even if he did leave home, he surely returned soon afterward. The evidence indicates that he attended school until he had almost reached the age of 14,[9] and moved to Subotica with his mother and sister in 1898. He began his stage acting career in Subotica in 1901.[10] His earliest provable performances are from provincial theatres in spring 1902, playing small roles in several plays and operettas.[11] He took the last name "Lugosi" in 1902 to honor his birthplace[5][12] (until 1911, the name was mostly spelled Lugosy, sometimes Lugosi, and more rarely Lugossy), and went on to perform in, among others, Shakespearean plays. After moving to Budapest in 1911, he played dozens of roles with the National Theatre of Hungary between 1913 and 1919. Although Lugosi would later claim that he "became the leading actor of Hungary's Royal National Theatre", most of his roles there were small or supporting parts, which led him to enter the Hungarian film industry.[13]

During World War I, he served in the Austro-Hungarian Army Imperial and Royal 43rd Infantry Regiment[14] from 1914 to 1916, with the rank of a corporal (in Austrian German: Zugsführer; in Hungarian: szakaszvezető[15]). He was probably awarded the Wound Medal for wounds he sustained while serving on the Russian front.[5] Returning to civilian life, Lugosi became an actor in Hungarian silent films, appearing in many of them under the stage name "Arisztid Olt".

Due to his activism in the actors' union in Hungary during the revolution of 1919 and his active participation in the Hungarian Soviet Republic,[16] he left his homeland when the government changed hands, initially accompanied by his first wife Ilona Szmik.[17][5] They escaped to Vienna before settling in Berlin (in the Langestrasse), where he began acting in German silent films. During these moves, Ilona lost her unborn child,[18] after which she left Lugosi and returned home to her parents, where she filed for divorce and soon after remarried.[5]

Lugosi eventually travelled to New Orleans, Louisiana, in December 1920 working as a crewman aboard a merchant ship, then made his way north to New York City, where he again took up acting in (and sometimes directing) stage plays in 1921–1922, then worked in the New York silent film industry from 1923 to 1926. In 1921, he met and married his second wife, Ilona von Montagh, a young Hungarian emigree and stage actress whom he had worked with years before in Europe. They only lived together for a few weeks, but their divorce was not finalized until October 1925.[19]

He later moved to California in 1928 to tour in the Dracula stage play, and his Hollywood film career took off. Lugosi claimed he performed the Dracula play around 1,000 times during his lifetime. He eventually became a U.S. citizen in 1931, soon after the release of his film version of Dracula.[17][5]

November Week 2 Nvidia Weekly Wrap

1. The board accepted Jensen Huang's resignation as president, CEO, and director on 11/11 and announced it on 11/12, after the Alice Huang (Megaspeed) allegations and a New York Times report of a separate relationship with health-care vice president Kimberly Powell. Colette Kress is interim CEO while remaining CFO, and Harvey Jones became the company's first board chair. The Wachtell Lipton independent investigation is continuing, and the board is maintaining that it has no basis to conclude that national security or trade secrets were compromised.

2. In an 11/13 statement to CNBC, the board said it is still choosing a search firm for the CEO role and has not formally approached any candidates. The Financial Times reported that the board approached Arm CEO Rene Haas. He is one of several candidates, and it is not settled whether he will get an offer or take it. Haas worked at Nvidia for seven years.

3. The Wall Street Journal reported that, as CFO, Kress cut a proposed $250 billion credit commitment for OpenAI's Ohio data center to an actual $105 billion guarantee. She questioned how credit-based deals should be valued and what returns they should earn, including deals involving Huang's son-in-law.

4. The stock closed at $162.85 on 11/13, down 2.01%, and fell about 13% on the week, its sixth straight weekly decline and the longest streak since 2012. Market value fell below $4 trillion for the first time since July 2025. HSBC downgraded the stock from buy to hold and cut its target to $170 from $365. It expects uncertainty to last until a permanent CEO is named, and says tighter export rules could cut FY28 EPS by 13%.

5. Fiscal 2027 third-quarter results are still due on 11/17 at 1:20 p.m. PT, with the call at 2:00 p.m. PT. Analysts surveyed by LSEG expect revenue of $108.9 billion. It will be the first call with Kress as interim CEO.

6. Senate Banking Chair Tim Scott asked Huang to testify on 12/3 and raised a subpoena if he refuses. Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick agreed to appear voluntarily on 12/10. The House China Select Committee sent a second request for a briefing, and Democrats who take control in January have promised more investigations. Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent publicly blamed Lutnick, saying Commerce held up adding Megaspeed to the Entity List for months. Axios also reported that Lutnick stalled a crackdown on chip diversion three times.

7. Reuters reported that it found about 23.2 billion yuan ($3.2 billion) of Chinese AI projects built around restricted Nvidia chips. The figure covers buildings and power systems, not just chips. The week added a leadership vacuum to an export-control fight that is now inside the administration.

text:
Last month I offered a seller $15,000 MORE than he was asking for his house, and walked away from the closing table with $0 out of my pocket

My realtor thought it was a typo on the contract

Here is how to use "seller credits" to make the seller and the bank pay 100% of your closing costs so you can buy a property with almost $0 cash

The house was a 3-bedroom brick ranch here in Ohio that had been sitting on Zillow for 68 days at $185,000

Structurally the place was solid, it just had a 1998 oak kitchen, beige carpet, and listing photos that looked like the seller's brother-in-law took them on an iPad with all the blinds closed

Most buyers see a house sitting for 2 months and try to lowball the seller at $170k

Problem is, even if the seller says yes to $170k, you still have to wire $12,000 to $15,000 out of your own bank account at closing just to pay the lender fees, title company, transfer taxes, insurance and property tax escrow

I hate wiring my own cash to title companies

So I sent him an offer for $200,000 ($15k over his asking price) with one line added to the contract:

"Seller to credit Buyer $15,000 at closing toward Buyer's closing costs, prepaids, and interest rate buydown"

He signed it in 20 minutes

The seller wanted $185,000. Getting $200,000 minus a $15,000 credit puts the exact same $185,000 in his pocket at closing (plus he gets to brag to his neighbors that he sold his house for $15k over asking)

On my side, a remodeled ranch with the same floorplan four doors down had just sold for $215,000, so the bank's appraiser walked through and easily appraised my house at $202,000

Because the loan was based on the $200k purchase price, the bank rolled that extra $15,000 straight into the mortgage

Do you know how much my monthly payment went up from adding $15k to the loan??

It actually dropped by $12 a month

Because we used $3,200 of the seller's $15,000 credit to buy 2 discount points on the loan (dropping the interest rate from 7% to 6.125%), and the other $11,800 paid every single penny of my title fees, lender charges, tax escrow and first year of homeowners insurance

If you want to run this on your next house or rental, follow these 4 rules so the bank doesn't reject it:

1. Hunt for ugly photos sitting 45+ days on Zillow. A seller in a bidding war on day 3 won't give you a credit, and a house already priced at the top of the street won't appraise $15k higher. Look for the dated house listed at $185k on a street where clean houses sell for $215k+ so the appraisal sails through

2. Check your loan's credit cap before you write the offer. Banks limit how much the seller is allowed to credit you based on the loan you use:
- FHA loans allow up to 6% of the price
- VA loans allow up to 4% (plus normal closing costs)
- Conventional homebuyer loans allow 3% (or 6% if you put 10%+ down)
- Conventional investor loans cap at 2%, which is why I use DSCR and local portfolio lenders on rentals that allow 3% to 6%

3. Never leave extra credit on the table. Seller credits are use-it-or-lose-it. If the seller gives you $15,000 and your closing bill is only $11,000, the bank won't let you pocket the leftover $4,000 as cash (it literally goes right back to the seller). Tell your loan officer to put every leftover dollar into buying down your interest rate or prepaying taxes, insurance and HOA

4. Put a 1-sentence appraisal shield in the contract. Write in: "If property appraises below $200,000, purchase price and seller credit shall reduce dollar-for-dollar to match appraised value" so you never get stuck overpaying if you get a grumpy appraiser

That $15k seller credit covered 100% of my closing costs and rate buydown

What about the down payment gap and the $14,000 we spent ripping out the beige carpet and updating the kitchen??

I didn't touch my personal checking account for that either

My purchase lender covered 80% of the house, and I put the down payment gap and the $14k remodel on 0% introductory business credit under my LLC (approved off my personal credit score, so those balances stay off my personal credit report while we finish the house, put a tenant in at $1,850 a month and refinance)

Most people with a 720 or 750 score sit on the sidelines for years trying to save up $50,000 in cash when their credit score can unlock the capital in 2 weeks

If you've got 700+ credit, I built a free calculator to estimate how much 0% introductory business funding you could qualify for before your next investment. Link in bio
