text:
The Shadow Kingdom: Analyzing the First Mythic/Fantasy Deep-State - Kull's Insecurities & Brule's Introduction to the First Great King in Mythic Literature

Here we are again. This time, we’re continuing with the deep dive into Robert E. Howard’s amazing Shadow Kingdom story, this one a tale that is as deep and frightening yet awesome as it is bleak and hopeful all at once. It being one of Howard and also Tolkien’s gifts to write a story that is capable of being both at once.

Let’s just dive in though, last time this story was analyzed in any great detail, it was in regards to the dinner to the feast so now we’re gonna close out that scene.

Ka-nu informs Kull of the need to trust Brule & him, and produces in an act meant to inspire good faith a bright emerald stone. The stone is one that the temple of Valusia prizes but seemingly lost, with Ka-nu assuring his liege of the Picts’ loyalties and their desire to ensure he stays King.

The feast though ends with Ka-nu telling him they’ll be in contact and pressing him to trust Brule. He follows that statement by dismissing the King, which is quite the bold thing to do.

““Tush. How impatient are youths!” Ka-nu looked more like a mischievous elf than ever. “Go you and dream of thrones and power and kingdoms, while I dream of wine and soft women and roses. And fortune ride with you, King Kull.””

What is so interesting about this dismissal is how this is the sort of act that Gandalf might have done with regards to the likes of Theoden and Denethor. It is an act that bespeaks to the influence of the Magician Archetype.

It seems to happen in literature if we’re being honest when the King suffers from the typical problems of being a King Archetype; that persistent hesitation/self-doubt the likes of which Theoden often suffers from and that is Kull’s continuous companion.

That said his remark about what dreams Kings have is interesting, it shows a certain scorn and bemusement towards those who seek thrones and power. It seems that Ka-nu is a man after Bilbo & Bombur’s own hearts even as he is someone who enjoys some measure of the joys (whatever they are) that power offers. A great lover of food, women and roses he cuts a very different sort of figure from most of Howard’s characters and also from most Magician Archetypes.

It is interesting how the Magician can as in the case of Mr. Miyagi, Ka-nu and even Biblo Baggins be a great lover of food, comfort and of all the material joys of life even as he stands apart from materialism.

This signals that the Archetype is not one that clings to materialism for its own sake, but only in how it can serve to enhance man and help set him at ease. It is only when we are at ease that we might work wonders after all, as societies that don’t provide a certain level of comfort are as we are discovering in large parts of the world proving incapable of creating noteworthy art.

What is also interesting is that what this means is that materialism of this sort can be put to the service of that which stands above materialism. This is something to bear in mind, and is a lesson that interestingly enough Pillars of the Earth also seems to preach (as it is an inadvertently Catholic work as noted by the brilliant Isaac Young during our podcast).

““You are young,” said the palaces and the temples and the shrines, “but we are old. The world was wild with youth when we were reared. You and your tribe shall pass, but we are invincible, indestructible. We towered above a strange world, ere Atlantis and Lemuria rose from the sea; we still shall reign when the green waters sigh for many a restless fathom above the spires of Lemuria and the hills of Atlantis and when the isles of the Western Men are the mountains of a strange land.”

This amazing paragraph comes after the scene in which Kull enjoys dinner with Ka-nu, with the story shifting to a very introspective and lore focused one. What Howard does in this part of the story is expand upon his world by mentioning that the towers of Valusia were already grand and large long before Lemuria and Atlantis even rose from the seas, which should tell us something of how old they are.

““How many kings have we watched ride down these streets before Kull of Atlantis was even a dream in the mind of Ka, bird of Creation? Ride on, Kull of Atlantis; greater shall follow you; greater came before you. They are dust; they are forgotten; we stand; we know; we are. Ride, ride on, Kull of Atlantis; Kull the king, Kull the fool!””

This is a fascinating boast on the part of the walls and towers of Valusia, with this one definitely coming in reality from deep within the great King. It happens that the hero is distressed at the thought that he might be nothing compared to Valusia.

He longs to have significance. Longs to prove himself worthy of Valusia, worthy to rule and worthy to save the nation he has come to love.

It is fascinating how the warrior is so insecure as to wonder if he is worthy of a city that has sunk into debauchery and chaos, and discord. It is interesting how he comes from without to save those within. Honestly, one can look at Kull as truly being a fictionalized version of the likes of Emperor Zeno of the Roman-Greek Empire in the east of Europe, and one whom proves himself no less remarkable and crucial to his nation’s destiny.

And yet Kull is not insane, this is simply what he thinks deep down just in mythologized form, this is what he says to himself, his claim to the throne is a weak one, and one that others have questioned and that is constantly pushed against so that Kull doubts and questions himself.

“And so in a brooding mood Kull came to the palace, where his bodyguard, men of the Red Slayers, came to take the rein of the great stallion and escort Kull to his rest. There the Pict, still sullenly speechless, wheeled his steed with a savage wrench of the rein and fled away in the dark like a phantom; Kull’s heightened imagination pictured him speeding through the silent streets like a goblin out of the Elder World.”

Naturally Kull by the time he returns home is annoyed by how alone he is in the world and how he is dwarfed by the magnificent structures of the ‘Elder World’ that is to say the realm over which he now Kings.

The man has a sense that he doesn’t belong and is a ‘goblin’ of sorts in this strange nation that has yet to fully accept him. A nation that regards him with mixed feelings, with mixed feelings. The people love him but the nobility despise him and consider him a foreign interloper.

Naturally once home Kull goes to bed, full of doubt yet sleeps the sleep of the sort of man who knows little joy and even less confidence in his place in the world. To say Kull is paranoid and miserable is to make the biggest understatement of the century.

It also merits asking is it in this situation really paranoia if they truly are out to get him?

It is interesting that at this point the relationship between Kull and Valusia is that akin to an abusive spouse wherein Valusia is over all kind of bad for Kull’s spiritual health and yet he clings to her throne with all the tenacity of a drowning man with drift wood.

Who should appear at this time but Brule the Spear-Slayer! Appearing just after Kull has awoken, girt his sword and wandered out he sweeps on in to present himself to Kull and to enlist his aid in the planned coup against the Snake-Men.

““I am Brule, the Spear-slayer,” answered the Pict in a guarded voice”

And so enters Brule, onto the scene as he introduces himself to the surprised Kull who did not know that the man he had met earlier was the Spear-Slayer he’s heard about from Ka-nu.

““Ka nama kaa lajerama!””

These are the words uttered next by Brule, why? To make certain that the King he is meeting with isn’t really a Snake-Person in disguise. He is eager to guard himself against the possibility of a fake/puppet of the Deep State that has wrecked so much ruin in Valusian history.

It happens that this is a ‘magic phrase’ of sorts that has an effect upon the Snake-Men who are immediately exposed for what they are. Snake-Men you see can take on the cover/identity of others and have used these illusory arts to control the Empire of Valusia for well over a thousand years.

Kull is shaken yet somehow recognizes the words, confirming that there is a common ancestor of sorts between most men which links back to early mythological and even Biblical beliefs about the origins of Man.

What it also does is allow us to see that this magic spell is one that is one that is familiar to all men on a genetic level almost while it is cancerous of sorts to the Snake-Men. The reason for this is that they are enemies on every level, and that they are supposed to be metaphysical opposites, spiritual enemies and completely and utterly opposed to one another.

text:
The Joyful Mysteries of the Rosary: Saturday November 14, 2026

A small house in Nazareth. A young woman at her tasks. An angel speaks, and the world turns on a yes she cannot yet measure. We know that pause. The day asks more than we meant to give. The Joyful Mysteries do not hide the fear. They show where joy begins, in a word trusted before the road is clear.

In the Annunciation, Mary receives the Word and offers her fiat. In the Visitation, she carries that Word to Elizabeth, and joy leaps before it is explained. At Bethlehem, God comes among us in poverty, not in display. In the Temple, Simeon and Anna recognize salvation in a child offered to the Father. Years later, Mary and Joseph find Jesus in his Father's house. He is already about his Father's affairs, and Mary keeps these things in her heart. These mysteries teach us that Christian joy is consent, service, humility, and a heart that seeks God. We pray the Joyful Mysteries with you today. Bring the unfinished yes, the hidden work, and the search that has gone on too long. Let Mary lead us to her Son.

I pray for you today 🙏 @RCatholicPrayer

text:
For centuries, a lamb was offered in Jerusalem each morning and another each afternoon. The daily offering. The tamid.

In the summer of AD 70, it stopped.

When Pompey's troops entered the Temple courts in 63 BC, Josephus says the priests kept offering sacrifices and were killed at the altar. The service continued under attack.

But during Titus's siege, Josephus records that the daily sacrifice failed "for want of men to offer it."

Titus sent Josephus to appeal to John of Gischala to let the service resume. John answered with curses.

The Temple was still standing. The altar was still there. But the daily offering had ceased. Within weeks, the sanctuary would burn.

In Stand in the Breach, that news reaches Roman headquarters as a line in the morning report. Something that had ordered generations of life in Jerusalem had become an item for the besiegers to record.

Pictured: the excavated "To the place of trumpeting" inscription from the Temple Mount, and the Temple's menorah and trumpets carried away in the relief on the Arch of Titus.

Ever seen a boat shaped like a giant basket? 🇮🇳😍

These are Coracles of Hampi, traditional circular boats made from woven bamboo and waterproofed with natural tar or resin.

Floating along the magnificent Tungabhadra River in Karnataka, these fascinating boats have been part of Hampi's river culture for generations.

Surrounded by enormous granite boulders, ancient Vijayanagara ruins and spectacular temple architecture, a coracle ride offers an unforgettable way to experience this UNESCO World Heritage landscape.

You can find these traditional rides near Virupaksha Temple, Kodandarama Temple, Chakratirtha and Sanapur Lake.

Ancient Indian ingenuity meets an extraordinary travel experience!

Would you take a ride in one of these? 🚣🇮🇳

text:
Here's a breakdown how the early Church Fathers and New Testament texts specifically framed the Church as the continuation of #Israel.

From an Orthodox perspective, the Church is not a "Plan B" or a separate Gentile entity running parallel to Israel; it is the historical continuation, restoration, and fulfillment of Israel in the Messiah.
Both the New Testament apostles and the earliest Church Fathers were unanimous on this point, arguing directly from the Hebrew Scriptures that covenant membership was always defined by faithfulness to God rather than mere physical descent.

1. The New Testament Foundation
The apostles systematically dismantled the idea of a dual-covenant system by redefining Israel around Christ Himself.

Christ as the True Israel:
In Matthew 2:15, the Evangelist applies Hosea 11:1 ("Out of Egypt I called my son") directly to #Jesus. Throughout the Gospels, Jesus recapitulates Israel's history—passing through the waters (baptism), enduring forty days in the wilderness, and appointing twelve apostles (Luke 22:30) specifically to reconstitute the twelve tribes of Israel.

The Olive Tree (Romans 9–11):
St. Paul explicitly states that "not all who are descended from Israel belong to Israel" (Romans 9:6). In Romans 11, he uses the image of a single cultivated olive tree: unbelieving branches were broken off, and believing Gentiles were grafted into the existing root of Israel. There is only one tree, not two.

Children of Abraham by Faith (Galatians 3 & 6):
Paul argues that God's promises were made to Abraham and his singular "offspring"—Christ (Galatians 3:16). Therefore, "if you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s offspring, heirs according to promise" (Galatians 3:29), concluding his epistle by calling the Church "the Israel of God" (Galatians 6:16).

Old Covenant Titles Transferred (1 Peter 2:9):
St. Peter takes the exact covenant titles bestowed upon Israel at Mount Sinai in Exodus 19:5–6 and applies them directly to the Church: "a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for his own possession."

The Synagogue of Satan (Revelation 2:9 & 3:9):
St. John writes to the churches in Smyrna and Philadelphia regarding those "who say that they are Jews and are not," establishing that rejecting the Messiah forfeits the spiritual claim to the covenant name.

In St. Paul's agricultural metaphor, wild Gentile branches do not form a separate orchard; they draw their life directly from the ancient patriarchs' rootstock.

2. The Early Church Fathers
Within a single generation of the apostles, the Fathers defended this exact ecclesiology against both Roman pagans and non-Christian Jewish polemicists, leaving zero room for modern dispensationalist distinctions.

St. Justin Martyrc. 160 ADDialogue with Trypho
Explicitly calls the Church "the true spiritual Israel" and descendants of Judah, Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham (Ch. 11).

St. Irenaeus of Lyons  c. 180 AD  Against Heresies
Teaches that the Church is the true seed of Abraham, inheriting the promises because the patriarchs rejoiced to see Christ's day (Book 4.8).

Tertullian   c. 200 AD  An Answer to the Jews  Argues from Rebecca's twins (Esau and Jacob) that the "older" people (Israel according to the flesh) now serve the "younger" people (the Church).

St. Cyprian of Carthage  c. 250 AD Three Books of Testimonies
Compiles dozens of Old Testament prophecies demonstrating that the Gentiles were foretold to inherit the vineyard and covenant of Israel.

Eusebius of Caesarea  c. 324 AD Church History
Traces the Church back to Abraham and the righteous pre-Mosaic patriarchs, showing Christianity is the original religion of Israel restored.

St. John Chrysostom  c. 387 AD Homilies on Galatians
Emphasizes that the "Israel of God" consists of those who walk by the rule of the Cross, whether Jew or Gentile by birth.

Key Patristic Arguments Against Sola Scriptura Proof-Texting
When modern Christian Zionists cite Old Testament land or blessing promises as unfulfilled guarantees for a modern secular state, they bypass how the Fathers read Scripture:

Typology and Fulfillment:
The Fathers read the Old Testament Christologically. The earthly Jerusalem, the Temple, and the land of Canaan were types (foreshadowings) pointing toward the Heavenly Jerusalem (Hebrews 12:22), the Body of Christ as the true Temple (John 2:21), and the entire cosmos redeemed in the Resurrection.

The "Remnant" Theology:
Drawing on Isaiah 10:22 and Romans 11:5, the Fathers pointed out that Israel was never completely cast off; rather, the faithful remnant of Israel—the Virgin Mary, the Twelve Apostles, the 3,000 baptized at Pentecost—became the foundation stones of the Church, into which the nations were then gathered.

Eucharistic Continuity:
Even the earliest liturgical manuals, such as the Didache (late 1st century), apply Malachi 1:11's prophecy of a "pure sacrifice" offered by the Gentiles directly to the Christian Eucharist, demonstrating that the Church understood itself from day one as offering the true, fulfilled worship of Israel.

Two programs enter this matchup with contrasting identities. Tennessee brings the more productive offense and a significantly stronger defensive profile, while Texas A&M offers a home-field advantage and a more possession-oriented approach. The statistical evidence reveals several important advantages on both sides.

text:
At its Worldwide Developer Conference on Monday, Apple for the first time unveiled its vision for supercharging its product lineup with artificial intelligence. The key feature, which will run across virtually all of its product line, is Apple Intelligence, a suite of AI-based capabilities that promises to deliver personalized AI services while keeping sensitive data secure.

It represents Apple’s largest leap forward in using our private data to help AI do tasks for us. To make the case it can do this without sacrificing privacy, the company says it has built a new way to handle sensitive data in the cloud.

Apple says its privacy-focused system will first attempt to fulfill AI tasks locally on the device itself. If any data is exchanged with cloud services, it will be encrypted and then deleted afterward. The company also says the process, which it calls Private Cloud Compute, will be subject to verification by independent security researchers. 

The pitch offers an implicit contrast with the likes of Alphabet, Amazon, or Meta, which collect and store enormous amounts of personal data. Apple says any personal data passed on to the cloud will be used only for the AI task at hand and will not be retained or accessible to the company, even for debugging or quality control, after the model completes the request. 

Simply put, Apple is saying people can trust it to analyze incredibly sensitive data—photos, messages, and emails that contain intimate details of our lives—and deliver automated services based on what it finds there, without actually storing the data online or making any of it vulnerable. 

It showed a few examples of how this will work in upcoming versions of iOS. Instead of scrolling through your messages for that podcast your friend sent you, for example, you could simply ask Siri to find and play it for you. Craig Federighi, Apple’s senior vice president of software engineering, walked through another scenario: an email comes in pushing back a work meeting, but his daughter is appearing in a play that night. His phone can now find the PDF with information about the performance, predict the local traffic, and let him know if he’ll make it on time. These capabilities will extend beyond apps made by Apple, allowing developers to tap into Apple’s AI too. 

Because the company profits more from hardware and services than from ads, Apple has less incentive than some other companies to collect personal online data, allowing it to position the iPhone as the most private device. Even so, Apple has previously found itself in the crosshairs of privacy advocates. Security flaws led to leaks of explicit photos from iCloud in 2014. In 2019, contractors were found to be listening to intimate Siri recordings for quality control. Disputes about how Apple handles data requests from law enforcement are ongoing. 

The first line of defense against privacy breaches, according to Apple, is to avoid cloud computing for AI tasks whenever possible. “The cornerstone of the personal intelligence system is on-device processing,” Federighi says, meaning that many of the AI models will run on iPhones and Macs rather than in the cloud. “It’s aware of your personal data without collecting your personal data.”

That presents some technical obstacles. Two years into the AI boom, pinging models for even simple tasks still requires enormous amounts of computing power. Accomplishing that with the chips used in phones and laptops is difficult, which is why only the smallest of Google’s AI models can be run on the company’s phones, and everything else is done via the cloud. Apple says its ability to handle AI computations on-device is due to years of research into chip design, leading to the M1 chips it began rolling out in 2020.

Yet even Apple’s most advanced chips can’t handle the full spectrum of tasks the company promises to carry out with AI. If you ask Siri to do something complicated, it may need to pass that request, along with your data, to models that are available only on Apple’s servers. This step, security experts say, introduces a host of vulnerabilities that may expose your information to outside bad actors, or at least to Apple itself.

“I always warn people that as soon as your data goes off your device, it becomes much more vulnerable,” says Albert Fox Cahn, executive director of the Surveillance Technology Oversight Project and practitioner in residence at NYU Law School’s Information Law Institute. 

Apple claims to have mitigated this risk with its new Private Cloud Computer system. “For the first time ever, Private Cloud Compute extends the industry-leading security and privacy of Apple devices into the cloud,” Apple security experts wrote in their announcement, stating that personal data “isn’t accessible to anyone other than the user—not even to Apple.” How does it work?

Historically, Apple has encouraged people to opt in to end-to-end encryption (the same type of technology used in messaging apps like Signal) to secure sensitive iCloud data. But that doesn’t work for AI. Unlike messaging apps, where a company like WhatsApp does not need to see the contents of your messages in order to deliver them to your friends, Apple’s AI models need unencrypted access to the underlying data to generate responses. This is where Apple’s privacy process kicks in. First, Apple says, data will be used only for the task at hand. Second, this process will be verified by independent researchers. 

Needless to say, the architecture of this system is complicated, but you can imagine it as an encryption protocol. If your phone determines it needs the help of a larger AI model, it will package a request containing the prompt it’s using and the specific model, and then put a lock on that request. Only the specific AI model to be used will have the proper key.

When asked by MIT Technology Review whether users will be notified when a certain request is sent to cloud-based AI models instead of being handled on-device, an Apple spokesperson said there will be transparency to users but that further details aren’t available.

Dawn Song, co-Director of UC Berkeley Center on Responsible Decentralized Intelligence and an expert in private computing, says Apple’s new developments are encouraging. “The list of goals that they announced is well thought out,” she says. “Of course there will be some challenges in meeting those goals.”

Cahn says that to judge from what Apple has disclosed so far, the system seems much more privacy-protective than other AI products out there today. That said, the common refrain in his space is “Trust but verify.” In other words, we won’t know how secure these systems keep our data until independent researchers can verify its claims, as Apple promises they will, and the company responds to their findings.

“Opening yourself up to independent review by researchers is a great step,” he says. “But that doesn’t determine how you’re going to respond when researchers tell you things you don’t want to hear.” Apple did not respond to questions from MIT Technology Review about how the company will evaluate feedback from researchers.

The privacy-AI bargain

Apple is not the only company betting that many of us will grant AI models mostly unfettered access to our private data if it means they could automate tedious tasks. OpenAI’s Sam Altman described his dream AI tool to MIT Technology Review as one “that knows absolutely everything about my whole life, every email, every conversation I’ve ever had.” At its own developer conference in May, Google announced Project Astra, an ambitious project to build a “universal AI agent that is helpful in everyday life.”

It’s a bargain that will force many of us to consider for the first time what role, if any, we want AI models to play in how we interact with our data and devices. When ChatGPT first came on the scene, that wasn’t a question we needed to ask. It was simply a text generator that could write us a birthday card or a poem, and the questions it raised—like where its training data came from or what biases it perpetuated—didn’t feel quite as personal. 

Now, less than two years later, Big Tech is making billion-dollar bets that we trust the safety of these systems enough to fork over our private information. It’s not yet clear if we know enough to make that call, or how able we are to opt out even if we’d like to. “I do worry that we’re going to see this AI arms race pushing ever more of our data into other people’s hands,” Cahn says.

Apple will soon release beta versions of its Apple Intelligence features, starting this fall with the iPhone 15 and the new macOS Sequoia, which can be run on Macs and iPads with M1 chips or newer. Says Apple CEO Tim Cook, “We think Apple intelligence is going to be indispensable.”

That opening works on someone comparing bookkeeping services. It means nothing to an owner who thinks their spreadsheet is working fine.

Same offer, different reader. So before you pick a copywriting formula or write a first line, figure out how much your reader already knows.

Copywriters often sort readers into five stages of awareness, from "doesn't know there's a problem" to "wants it, needs a reason to act now." The less your reader knows, the more ground the copy has to cover before it mentions your offer. The more they know, the sooner you can get to proof, price, and the ask.

The image shows one bookkeeping service opening five different ways, one for each stage.

Treat the stages as a starting point, not a script. A problem-first email can work fine on people who know your brand well. Just don't open with features for a reader who doesn't know yet why they'd need them.

text:
Google is set to introduce a new system called Astra later this year and promises that it will be the most powerful, advanced type of AI assistant it’s ever launched. 

The current generation of AI assistants, such as ChatGPT, can retrieve information and offer answers, but that is about it. But this year, Google is rebranding its assistants as more advanced “agents,” which it says could  show reasoning, planning, and memory skills and are able to take multiple steps to execute tasks. 

People will be able to use Astra through their smartphones and possibly desktop computers, but the company is exploring other options too, such as embedding it into smart glasses or other devices, Oriol Vinyals, vice president of research at Google DeepMind, told MIT Technology Review. 

“We are in very early days [of AI agent development],” Google CEO Sundar Pichai said on a call ahead of Google’s I/O conference today. 

“We’ve always wanted to build a universal agent that will be useful in everyday life,” said Demis Hassabis, the CEO and cofounder of Google DeepMind. “Imagine agents that can see and hear what we do, better understand the context we’re in, and respond quickly in conversation, making the pace and quality of interaction feel much more natural.” That, he says, is what Astra will be. 

Google’s announcement comes a day after competitor OpenAI unveiled its own supercharged AI assistant, GPT-4o. Google DeepMind’s Astra responds to audio and video inputs, much in the same way as GPT-4o (albeit it less flirtatiously). 

In a press demo, a user pointed a smartphone camera and smart glasses at things and asked Astra to explain what they were. When the person pointed the device out the window and asked “What neighborhood do you think I’m in?” the AI system was able to identify King’s Cross, London, site of Google DeepMind’s headquarters. It was also able to say that the person’s glasses were on a desk, having recorded them earlier in the interaction. 

The demo showcases Google DeepMind’s vision of multimodal AI (which can handle multiple types of input—voice, video, text, and so on) working in real time, Vinyals says. 

“We are very excited about, in the future, to be able to really just get closer to the user, assist the user with anything that they want,” he says. Google recently upgraded its artificial-intelligence model Gemini to process even larger amounts of data, an upgrade which helps it handle bigger documents and videos, and have longer conversations. 

Tech companies are in the middle of a fierce competition over AI supremacy, and  AI agents are the latest effort from Big Tech firms to show they are pushing the frontier of development. Agents also play into a narrative by many tech companies, including OpenAI and Google DeepMind, that aim to build artificial general intelligence, a highly hypothetical idea of superintelligent AI systems. 

“Eventually, you’ll have this one agent that really knows you well, can do lots of things for you, and can work across multiple tasks and domains,” says Chirag Shah, a professor at the University of Washington who specializes in online search.

This vision is still aspirational. But today’s announcement should be seen as Google’s attempt to keep up with competitors. And by rushing these products out, Google can collect even more data from its over a billion users on how they are using their models and what works, Shah says.

Google is unveiling many more new AI capabilities beyond agents today. It’s going to integrate AI more deeply into Search through a new feature called AI overviews, which gather information from the internet and package them into short summaries in response to search queries. The feature, which launches today, will initially be available only in the US, with more countries to gain access later. 

This will help speed up the search process and get users more specific answers to more complex, niche questions, says Felix Simon, a research fellow in AI and digital news at the Reuters Institute for Journalism. “I think that’s where Search has always struggled,” he says. 

Another new feature of Google’s AI Search offering is better planning. People will soon be able to ask Search to make meal and travel suggestions, for example, much like asking a travel agent to suggest restaurants and hotels. Gemini will be able to help them plan what they need to do or buy to cook recipes, and they will also be able to have conversations with the AI system, asking it to do anything from relatively mundane tasks, such as informing them about the weather forecast, to highly complex ones like helping them prepare for a job interview or an important speech. 

People will also be able to interrupt Gemini midsentence and ask clarifying questions, much as in a real conversation. 

In another move to one-up competitor OpenAI, Google also unveiled Veo, a new video-generating AI system. Veo is able to generate short videos and allows users more control over cinematic styles by understanding prompts like “time lapse” or “aerial shots of a landscape.”

Google has a significant advantage when it comes to training generative video models, because it owns YouTube. It’s already announced collaborations with artists such as Donald Glover and Wycleaf Jean, who are using its technology to produce their work. 

Earlier this year, OpenA’s CTO, Mira Murati, fumbled when asked about whether the company’s model was trained on YouTube data. Douglas Eck, senior research director at Google DeepMind, was also vague about the training data used to create Veo when asked about by MIT Technology Review, but he said that it “may be trained on some YouTube content in accordance with our agreements with YouTube creators.”

On one hand, Google is presenting its generative AI as a tool artists can use to make stuff, but the tools likely get their ability to create that stuff by using material from existing artists, says Shah. AI companies such as Google and OpenAI have faced a slew of lawsuits by writers and artists claiming that their intellectual property has been used without consent or compensation.  

“For artists it’s a double-edged sword,” says Shah.

text:
Today, I followed a number of recent interviews with senior Iranian leaders and officials at the political and security levels. This type of interview reveals an important aspect of the transformations in Iranian strategic thinking after the wars of 2025 and 2026—politically, security-wise, militarily, and diplomatically—and in the way war and negotiations are managed.

In my view, Iran cannot be understood through its official institutions alone. It also requires a deeper examination of the visions of its leaders, their direct and indirect statements, and the alliances, currents, and different camps within the system, as well as their differing assessments of threats, opportunities, and ways of dealing with them.

The conclusion I drew from these interviews regarding Iran’s view of war, negotiations, the United States, Israel, and the region in general is that there are a number of shared constants in Iranian discourse, despite the different positions and political, intellectual, and ideological backgrounds of the speakers.

1.The speakers do not practically distinguish between any American or Israeli attack. Israel is presented as the instigator or operational partner, while the United States is portrayed as the power providing it with military, political, and economic cover.

2.The current calm is not presented as stable peace, but rather as a state of “neither war nor peace” and a truce that could collapse. Therefore, the Iranian vision seeks to prevent a return to the rules that prevailed before the war and to establish new deterrence equations.

3.Mohammad Reza Naqdi stated clearly that neither war nor negotiations are ends in themselves. The criterion here is to build deterrence that makes the adversary realize that the cost of attacking Iran would be greater than any expected gain.

4.Both Mohebi and Rezaei directly offer a clear definition of deterrence: the aggressor must pay a military, political, and economic price that makes him reconsider before repeating an attack. This is the essence of deterrence by punishment, as we studied it in strategic studies.

5.None of them rejects negotiations in principle. Rather, they reject negotiations that begin with weakening Iran or stripping it of its instruments of power. In their view, acceptable negotiations are those that come after an American recognition of what Tehran considers its legitimate rights and interests.

6.The shared discourse stresses that Washington must first undertake tangible measures, rather than demand initial concessions from Iran. Here, Iran seeks to reverse the traditional formula: implementation and guarantees before negotiations, not promises in exchange for concessions.

7. There is a shared invocation of the August 1953 coup, sanctions, the assassination of General Qassem Soleimani in Baghdad, the withdrawal from the nuclear agreement, and the joint attack during negotiations in Geneva and Oman, in order to demonstrate that, from the Iranian perspective, the problem is not linked to a specific American administration, but rather to a recurring American pattern.

8.Rezaei rejected the removal of enriched materials from Iran or the abandonment of rights that Tehran considers guaranteed under the Treaty on the Non-Proliferation of Nuclear Weapons. Therefore, the shared discourse rejects turning the nuclear file into a gateway for reducing Iran’s broader strategic capacity.

9.All the speakers place the Strait of Hormuz within the context of war, blockade, sanctions, and political conditions. Therefore, opening it or regulating navigation through it is no longer presented as a separate maritime issue, but as part of a new security and political arrangement in the Gulf and the region in general.

The Somali Bar Association’s Sham Defense of Hassan Sheikh Mohamud: A Betrayal of Judicial Independence and the Rule of Law

Conspicuously absent from public debate over Somalia’s prolonged constitutional crisis, the Somali Bar Association (SBA) has suddenly emerged to defend the unconstitutional actions of Hassan Sheikh Mohamud. In its 11 November 2026 response to the East Africa Law Society (EALS), the SBA dismissed urgent regional concerns regarding judicial independence, the safety of judicial officers, and the rule of law in the Federal Republic of Somalia following the unlawful removal of Supreme Court Chief Justice Baashe Yusuf Ahmed and the persecution of fellow Supreme Court justices. Rather than confronting executive abuse, the SBA offered procedural excuses and a flawed interpretation of presidential authority that directly undermines the constitutional principles it exists to uphold.

At the heart of this crisis lies a fundamental constitutional question: Can a president whose mandate expired on 15 May 2026—following the expiration of the Federal Parliament’s mandate on 14 April—dismiss the Chief Justice while his own legitimacy is under judicial review, reject final court rulings, and deploy state security forces to enforce his political will?

The Constitutional Crisis and the Supreme Court’s Rulings

The crisis stems from unilateral constitutional amendments passed in March 2026 to establish a state-sponsored political party, manipulate the electoral system, and extend federal mandates from four to five years. On 11 October 2026, former President Sharif Sheikh Ahmed—a presidential candidate whose political rights were infringed by the failure to hold the elections scheduled for May 2026—petitioned the Supreme Court, challenging both the amendment process and the resulting mandate extensions. Although the Attorney General filed preliminary objections questioning the petitioner’s standing and the Court’s jurisdiction, the Court expressly examined and ruled on both issues in its written judgment.

On 4 November, as the Court prepared to deliver its decision, Villa Somalia announced on Facebook that Hassan Sheikh Mohamud had dismissed Chief Justice Baashe Yusuf Ahmed and appointed former Chief Justice Ibrahim Idle Suleiman, an ardent, card-carrying member of the ruling Justice and Solidarity Party (JSP). Security forces immediately intervened at the Court, restricting judges’ movements, withdrawing their security protection, and interfering with digital systems.

The timing exposed a blatant conflict of interest: a president whose continuation in office was under judicial review removed the head of the Court in an apparent attempt to preempt an unfavorable verdict.

On 5 November, a five-judge Constitutional Division panel issued its ruling in the presence of Chief Justice Baashe Yusuf Ahmed. Asserting jurisdiction under Article 191(3) of the revised 2026 Constitution, the Court dismissed the challenge to the amendment procedure under Article 86 but recognized the petitioner’s standing to challenge the retrospective extension of mandates. It ruled that:

Constitutional amendments extending the duration of elected offices cannot automatically apply retrospectively to incumbents.
The mandates of the Federal Parliament (14 April 2026) and the President (15 May 2026) had expired, restricting the Federal Cabinet to strictly routine caretaker functions.
Political stakeholders must agree on an acceptable electoral framework within 30 days and conduct elections within 90 days.

That same day, the Court formally declared the Chief Justice’s dismissal unconstitutional, null, and void, citing Articles 135 and 138 of the revised Constitution, which require the involvement of the Judicial Council and Parliament—not a unilateral presidential decree.

text:
Before Fernando Mendoza won the @HeismanTrophy last year, his mom, Elsa, wrote him a heartfelt letter: “You’ve had to overcome obstacles at every step along the way — and I’m so proud of how, instead of letting those obstacles define you, you’ve treated them as opportunities to define yourself.

I always think about year one of park football, when you were the new kid in town, and told your coaches that you wanted to play quarterback. They said, ‘OK……… But you’re QB4 right now.’ You said, ‘That’s fine.’ Then you worked hard, and stayed patient. And when you eventually got to take some snaps, big surprise, you played great!

I think about 9th grade, when you were at a school that you loved … but the football team ran a Wing-T offense. And after the season, you came to me and your dad and were like, ‘Guys, I think I can play college football. And if I’m going to have a chance at that, I need to develop as a QB. And to develop as a QB, I need to play in a pro-style offense.’ So you switched schools for 10th grade, which really came at a cost. A lot of your friends disowned you for a while … people called you a traitor … it broke your heart. But you knew what you wanted, so you made the difficult choice.

I think about Covid, and how it hit when you were just starting to play so well. You guys had a shot at a state championship that season — and it got canceled!!! I was devastated for you. And it impacted your recruiting, too, with all the restrictions in place. They had you rated as a two-star prospect (which I never believed), so no Power 5 offers were coming. But you just refused to give up. You went to camp after camp after camp that summer, I think 17 in all. And after a while we basically became each other’s hype man. I’d be like, ‘Fernando, you’re going to get a Power 5 offer. I’m telling you.’ And you’d be like, ‘I’m gonna do it, Mami. I’m gonna do it, I know it.’ And then you did it.

And finally, I think about last year, when you made the decision to transfer from Cal. I know how much you cherished your time there…… you’re a true ‘Golden Bear,’ with the amazing degree to prove it!! But I also know, at a certain point, that you had another goal in mind: to make the NFL. And in talking to Alberto about his development at IU, you became convinced that playing for Coach Cignetti and his staff was the right path forward. I saw how it all weighed on you, though — and how at first you almost felt bad for having fun in Bloomington, because a piece of your heart was still in Berkeley. But to me that’s one of your best qualities. You have a tenderness about you that I think is rare in sports. And eventually you realized what I knew you would: We move through life in chapters! And enjoying the chapter we’re on now doesn’t diminish the one we were on before.” https://t.co/EGwjsSKeX8

text:
China will pay you more than $15,000 to report a spy. The bounty program is run by China's spy agency, the Ministry of State Security, which recently had to warn the public not to use it on coworkers. It's the same agency that The New York Times reported recruited a businesswoman named Alice Huang to spy on Jensen Huang, the CEO of Nvidia.

A small clue merits a reward of up to 10,000 yuan (about $1,500), according to guidelines published by the ministry; particularly important intelligence can net over a hundred thousand yuan (about $15,000). No ceiling is written down. China's counter-espionage law requires all Chinese citizens who discover spy activities to report them.

Every April, the ministry announces the year's most valuable informants; this year, the number reached an all-time high of 103. One of them was a ride-hailing driver named Chen, who noticed that two foreigners he was transporting were repeatedly taking photos of a military barracks gate and called the spy hotline to report them. When they hired him again, he drove toward the gate of the barracks, suddenly braked, and grabbed their phone. He received the top reward from the ministry.

One of the cases that the ministry publicized recently involved the opposite situation. A top graduate named Liu worked at a state-sponsored institution and, in 2024, applied for a job abroad. So did one of his colleagues. According to the ministry, Liu was confident that he would get it. But the institution chose his colleague instead.

Liu's motive, the ministry said, was jealousy: he penned an anonymous letter to an overseas organization, accusing that colleague of being a spy and hoping to make trouble for him before he moved abroad for work. The ministry uncovered the plot and gave Liu an administrative warning, its lightest sanction.

It isn't an isolated case. The ministry revealed a similar case in 2025, when an employee of a provincial government, Yan, accused a colleague he had hated for years by mimicking a real espionage case. The colleague, who worked in a position that required a security clearance, was investigated but eventually exonerated. Yan was demoted.

Chen the driver and Liu both resorted to China's most serious accusation. When the government offers rewards for espionage tips and holds out reporting as a civic duty, it gives everyone the one accusation that the authorities cannot ignore, and, in most cases, that they cannot know is false or malicious until after they have investigated the target. The ministry ended its most recent warning with a call for people to keep reporting.

text:
China’s Belt and Road Initiative (BRI) has made the Middle East one of its top regions for construction contracts and investment, focusing on ports, industrial zones, energy (oil/gas and renewables), transport, and manufacturing. In 2024 the region led globally with roughly $39 billion in BRI deals (up sharply year-on-year); 2025 figures show continued strength, with Middle East construction engagement around $39.4 billion (second worldwide). Saudi Arabia, Iraq, the UAE, and Egypt have been the largest recipients.⁠Agbi⁠Zawya

Nearly all Middle Eastern countries (about 20 of 22) have signed BRI cooperation documents. Cumulative Chinese construction contracts since the BRI’s 2013 launch exceed $100 billion in the GCC alone, plus substantial amounts in Iraq and Iran.

Analysts and Western governments highlight latent dual-use features for several reasons:
Chinese legal and policy framework: Laws such as the National Defense Transportation Law require Chinese firms and overseas infrastructure to support military needs (resupply, personnel rest, logistics) when requested for operations defending national interests, anti-piracy, or related missions. This reflects a military-civil fusion approach.⁠Jiia
Logistics and access: Chinese-operated or invested ports can facilitate PLAN (People’s Liberation Army Navy) port calls for fuel, maintenance, or diplomacy. PLAN vessels have visited ports in the UAE, Oman, Saudi Arabia, and others. In a crisis, commercial terminals could support longer-term logistics without a formal base.
Intelligence and surveillance: Terminal operations, sensors, equipment (including some Chinese-made cranes or digital systems), and personnel can enable collection on shipping, regional militaries, or movements. Proximity to US/partner bases adds value (e.g., Khalifa near Al Dhafra and Jebel Ali).
Strategic positioning: Facilities near chokepoints (Hormuz, Red Sea/Bab el-Mandeb approaches) offer potential leverage or support for energy security and power projection. The “first civilian, then military” pattern seen in Djibouti is cited as a model, though it has not been replicated at scale in the Gulf.
Notable specific cases:
Khalifa Port (UAE): In 2021, US intelligence flagged suspected Chinese construction activity linked to a potential military facility. The UAE reportedly halted work under US pressure; later reports (including from leaked documents) suggested possible resumption or continued concerns. No confirmed permanent Chinese base exists. The port remains a major commercial hub with a COSCO terminal.⁠Atlanticcouncil
Duqm Port (Oman): Chinese investment in the port and special economic zone has raised speculation about future access due to its location outside the Strait of Hormuz and infrastructure capable of supporting naval vessels. It is primarily commercial; Oman balances relations with multiple powers (including UK facilities at the port). No confirmed Chinese military base.⁠Isdp
Djibouti: Commercial port and free-zone investments preceded China’s 2017 military logistics base, which supports anti-piracy, resupply, and broader presence near the Red Sea. This is the clearest dual-use/military outcome linked to BRI-style development in the broader region.
Other ports (e.g., Chinese involvement around Haifa in Israel) have drawn US concerns over docking of naval vessels and potential equipment-related risks.
Energy, Industrial, and Other Facilities
Oil/gas refineries, power plants, solar/wind projects, railways, and manufacturing zones have far lower dual-use military relevance than ports. Digital infrastructure (Huawei and related 5G/smart-city work) raises separate concerns about data security and potential intelligence access, distinct from traditional dual-use port logistics.
Overall Assessment
Current reality: Facilities are overwhelmingly civilian. Permanent Chinese military basing in the Gulf or Egypt has not materialized, partly due to host governments’ security ties with the US and others, and Beijing’s preference for lower-profile commercial access.
Potential: Ports offer dual-use utility for logistics and intelligence without needing full bases. This fits China’s broader maritime strategy of building a global port network that can support naval operations when needed, subject to host permission.
China describes the projects as purely commercial and notes that military use depends on sovereign host approval. Western assessments treat the dual-use risk as real and strategically relevant near energy routes and chokepoints, even without overt bases.
In short, these are not dual-use military bases today, but key ports have inherent or potential dual-use characteristics that US and partner governments monitor closely.

text:
Here's a breakdown how the early Church Fathers and New Testament texts specifically framed the Church as the continuation of #Israel.

From an Orthodox perspective, the Church is not a "Plan B" or a separate Gentile entity running parallel to Israel; it is the historical continuation, restoration, and fulfillment of Israel in the Messiah. 
Both the New Testament apostles and the earliest Church Fathers were unanimous on this point, arguing directly from the Hebrew Scriptures that covenant membership was always defined by faithfulness to God rather than mere physical descent.

1. The New Testament Foundation
The apostles systematically dismantled the idea of a dual-covenant system by redefining Israel around Christ Himself.

Christ as the True Israel:
 In Matthew 2:15, the Evangelist applies Hosea 11:1 ("Out of Egypt I called my son") directly to #Jesus. Throughout the Gospels, Jesus recapitulates Israel's history—passing through the waters (baptism), enduring forty days in the wilderness, and appointing twelve apostles (Luke 22:30) specifically to reconstitute the twelve tribes of Israel.

The Olive Tree (Romans 9–11):
 St. Paul explicitly states that "not all who are descended from Israel belong to Israel" (Romans 9:6). In Romans 11, he uses the image of a single cultivated olive tree: unbelieving branches were broken off, and believing Gentiles were grafted into the existing root of Israel. There is only one tree, not two.

Children of Abraham by Faith (Galatians 3 & 6): 
Paul argues that God's promises were made to Abraham and his singular "offspring"—Christ (Galatians 3:16). Therefore, "if you are Christ’s, then you are Abraham’s offspring, heirs according to promise" (Galatians 3:29), concluding his epistle by calling the Church "the Israel of God" (Galatians 6:16).

Old Covenant Titles Transferred (1 Peter 2:9): 
St. Peter takes the exact covenant titles bestowed upon Israel at Mount Sinai in Exodus 19:5–6 and applies them directly to the Church: "a chosen race, a royal priesthood, a holy nation, a people for his own possession."

The Synagogue of Satan (Revelation 2:9 & 3:9): 
St. John writes to the churches in Smyrna and Philadelphia regarding those "who say that they are Jews and are not," establishing that rejecting the Messiah forfeits the spiritual claim to the covenant name.

In St. Paul's agricultural metaphor, wild Gentile branches do not form a separate orchard; they draw their life directly from the ancient patriarchs' rootstock.

2. The Early Church Fathers
Within a single generation of the apostles, the Fathers defended this exact ecclesiology against both Roman pagans and non-Christian Jewish polemicists, leaving zero room for modern dispensationalist distinctions.

St. Justin Martyrc. 160 ADDialogue with Trypho
Explicitly calls the Church "the true spiritual Israel" and descendants of Judah, Jacob, Isaac, and Abraham (Ch. 11).

St. Irenaeus of Lyons  c. 180 AD  Against Heresies
Teaches that the Church is the true seed of Abraham, inheriting the promises because the patriarchs rejoiced to see Christ's day (Book 4.8).

Tertullian   c. 200 AD  An Answer to the Jews  Argues from Rebecca's twins (Esau and Jacob) that the "older" people (Israel according to the flesh) now serve the "younger" people (the Church).

St. Cyprian of Carthage  c. 250 AD Three Books of Testimonies 
Compiles dozens of Old Testament prophecies demonstrating that the Gentiles were foretold to inherit the vineyard and covenant of Israel.

Eusebius of Caesarea  c. 324 AD Church History 
Traces the Church back to Abraham and the righteous pre-Mosaic patriarchs, showing Christianity is the original religion of Israel restored.

St. John Chrysostom  c. 387 AD Homilies on Galatians 
Emphasizes that the "Israel of God" consists of those who walk by the rule of the Cross, whether Jew or Gentile by birth.

Key Patristic Arguments Against Sola Scriptura Proof-Texting
When modern Christian Zionists cite Old Testament land or blessing promises as unfulfilled guarantees for a modern secular state, they bypass how the Fathers read Scripture:

Typology and Fulfillment: 
The Fathers read the Old Testament Christologically. The earthly Jerusalem, the Temple, and the land of Canaan were types (foreshadowings) pointing toward the Heavenly Jerusalem (Hebrews 12:22), the Body of Christ as the true Temple (John 2:21), and the entire cosmos redeemed in the Resurrection.

The "Remnant" Theology: 
Drawing on Isaiah 10:22 and Romans 11:5, the Fathers pointed out that Israel was never completely cast off; rather, the faithful remnant of Israel—the Virgin Mary, the Twelve Apostles, the 3,000 baptized at Pentecost—became the foundation stones of the Church, into which the nations were then gathered.

Eucharistic Continuity: 
Even the earliest liturgical manuals, such as the Didache (late 1st century), apply Malachi 1:11's prophecy of a "pure sacrifice" offered by the Gentiles directly to the Christian Eucharist, demonstrating that the Church understood itself from day one as offering the true, fulfilled worship of Israel.

text:
“ Ezekiel 27:5, in the lament over Tyre, says: “They made all your planking of pine trees from Senir; they took a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you”. The once-proud maritime city is portrayed through a lavishly built vessel whose splendid mast could not save her from ruin (Ezekiel 27:27).”
✝️🔥🔥🔥
“The word of the LORD came to me: “Son of man, take up a lament concerning Tyre. Say to Tyre, situated at the gateway to the sea, merchant of peoples on many coasts, ‘This is what the Sovereign LORD says: “ ‘You say, Tyre, “I am perfect in beauty.” Your domain was on the high seas; your builders brought your beauty to perfection. They made all your timbers of juniper from Senir; they took a cedar from Lebanon to make a mast for you. Of oaks from Bashan they made your oars; of cypress wood from the coasts of Cyprus they made your deck, adorned with ivory. Fine embroidered linen from Egypt was your sail and served as your banner; your awnings were of blue and purple from the coasts of Elishah. Men of Sidon and Arvad were your oarsmen; your skilled men, Tyre, were aboard as your sailors. Veteran craftsmen of Byblos were on board as shipwrights to caulk your seams. All the ships of the sea and their sailors came alongside to trade for your wares. “ ‘Men of Persia, Lydia and Put served as soldiers in your army. They hung their shields and helmets on your walls, bringing you splendor. Men of Arvad and Helek guarded your walls on every side; men of Gammad were in your towers. They hung their shields around your walls; they brought your beauty to perfection. “ ‘Tarshish did business with you because of your great wealth of goods; they exchanged silver, iron, tin and lead for your merchandise. “ ‘Greece, Tubal and Meshek did business with you; they traded human beings and articles of bronze for your wares. “ ‘Men of Beth Togarmah exchanged chariot horses, cavalry horses and mules for your merchandise. “ ‘The men of Rhodes traded with you, and many coastlands were your customers; they paid you with ivory tusks and ebony. “ ‘Aram did business with you because of your many products; they exchanged turquoise, purple fabric, embroidered work, fine linen, coral and rubies for your merchandise. “ ‘Judah and Israel traded with you; they exchanged wheat from Minnith and confections, honey, olive oil and balm for your wares. “ ‘Damascus did business with you because of your many products and great wealth of goods. They offered wine from Helbon, wool from Zahar and casks of wine from Izal in exchange for your wares: wrought iron, cassia and calamus. “ ‘Dedan traded in saddle blankets with you. “ ‘Arabia and all the princes of Kedar were your customers; they did business with you in lambs, rams and goats. “ ‘The merchants of Sheba and Raamah traded with you; for your merchandise they exchanged the finest of all kinds of spices and precious stones, and gold. “ ‘Harran, Kanneh and Eden and merchants of Sheba, Ashur and Kilmad traded with you. In your marketplace they traded with you beautiful garments, blue fabric, embroidered work and multicolored rugs with cords twisted and tightly knotted. “ ‘The ships of Tarshish serve as carriers for your wares. You are filled with heavy cargo as you sail the sea. Your oarsmen take you out to the high seas. But the east wind will break you to pieces far out at sea. Your wealth, merchandise and wares, your mariners, sailors and shipwrights, your merchants and all your soldiers, and everyone else on board will sink into the heart of the sea on the day of your shipwreck. The shorelands will quake when your sailors cry out. All who handle the oars will abandon their ships; the mariners and all the sailors will stand on the shore. They will raise their voice and cry bitterly over you; they will sprinkle dust on their heads and roll in ashes. They will shave their heads because of you and will put on sackcloth.
👇👇👇

text:
Most Americans retire at 65

Kevin Federline retired at 29, the year he divorced Britney Spears

His pension ran for 17 years

It ended in November 2024. That same month, he opened a credit card

Now the bank is suing him for $117,704

But the bank isn't the twist

A year ago, Kevin sat down in front of a camera and told America this was NEVER about money

When they split, he got the boys and she got the bills. Tens of thousands of dollars a month, for almost two decades, while Britney was stuck in a conservatorship and couldn't even control her own bank account

Then the boys grew up and the payments ended

Less than a year later, Kevin released a memoir about her

Claims about drugs, knives and what the boys saw in her house. Britney's team said the timing told you everything: the book came out right after the money stopped. Britney answered herself: "You profit off my pain"

Kevin sat down with TV crews at his home in Hawaii and pushed back. He said he'd been offered seven figures for interviews over the years and turned them all down. He said he only waited so his kids would be old enough to understand

Now the bank says the credit card, the credit line and the checking account he opened right after the support ended all went unpaid

It isn't the first one. Earlier this year Bank of America took him to court too. That case quietly went away after he paid

The case for Kevin: he raised two boys the whole world was watching, he says most of that money went to security and nannies, and he has six kids to feed

The case against: he lived on his ex-wife's money for 17 years, then sold her worst moments the minute it ran out

In the video below, he's asked straight out if he wrote the book because Britney's money stopped

Listen to his answer, then think about that lawsuit

If someone supported you for 17 years, do you owe them your silence when the money stops?

text:
I'm an immigrant to the United States, and let me tell you something.

America is NOT a nation of immigrants. 

Nor should it be.

One of the most dangerous, sovereignty-eroding ideas floating around today is that "America is a nation of immigrants."

I used to be inspired by messaging like this.

But now I realize how evil that idea truly is.

No. Thank you.

We are a nation of Americans. And we are a nation of laws.

The vast majority of Americans are not immigrants. Roughly 85% of people living in this country were born here. An immigrant, by definition, is someone who comes here from another country. When more than eight in ten people were born on American soil, you are not a nation of immigrants. You are a nation of Americans.

And that is the entire idea of America. When you come here, follow the laws, assimilate, and take part in the American story, you BECOME an American. Ronald Reagan put it best in his final speech as president (see video):

"You can go to live in France, but you cannot become a Frenchman. You can go to live in Germany or Turkey or Japan, but you cannot become a German, a Turk, or a Japanese. But anyone, from any corner of the Earth, can come to live in America and become an American."

That's a rare kind of national identity. Very few countries offer it to the people of the world, and the ones that do haven't done it nearly as well as America has.

Making up labels like "first gen," "second gen," and so on doesn't turn people into immigrants. If you were born on US soil and you participate in American values, culture, and way of life, you are an American.

Period.

In fact, the "nation of immigrants" framing works against the very idea that anyone can come here and become an American. It quietly suggests that belonging is about ancestry, that you're defined forever by where your parents or grandparents came from. That is the logic of blood and soil, the logic of white supremacists, and we should want nothing to do with it.

If we want to rebuild a shared national identity around being American, we have to reject:

- othering certain groups of people
- the divide-and-conquer strategy
- the obsession with ethnicity
- the obsession with race
- the obsession with division

Here's why I worry so deeply about this. 

When you divide a population, it fractures, and then those fractures splinter into more factions. 

The founders saw this danger coming. In Federalist No. 10, James Madison defined a faction as:

"a number of citizens, whether amounting to a majority or a minority of the whole, who are united and actuated by some common impulse of passion, or of interest, adverse to the rights of other citizens, or to the permanent and aggregate interests of the community."

Voting blocs organized around ethnicity are exactly that kind of faction. They pull people toward the interests of their group and away from the long-term good of the nation. This matters.

Now, I say all this because I BELIEVE in immigration. We should remain a country where people from anywhere, seeking freedom, refuge, and opportunity, can come to these shores and build a better life. I did.

But here's what people get wrong. Being an American citizen and being an American are two different things.

Citizenship is a legal status. You apply, you meet the requirements, you pass the test, and you take the oath. We are a nation of laws, and that process matters.

Being an American is something else. It's whether you actually BELIEVe in THIS country and live like it. The paperwork doesn't give you that. You have to choose it.

We should want both.

And most people already have both. Immigrants are only about 15% of the population, and half of them are already naturalized citizens. That means only about 7% of people living here aren't American citizens yet.

That is not a nation of immigrants.

We are a nation of Americans.

text:
There is a certain nuance to the argument I am trying to make, so allow me to clarify. In trying to modernise James Bond, the reboot's films sanded away much of the polished, gentlemanly quality from the character. As a result, Daniel Craig's Bond lacks an important contrast present in the portrayals of the other five actors.

In the novels, Bond is a study in duality: a gentleman and a killer. One senses that, though he takes no pleasure in killing, he takes pride in carrying out his professional duties with precision. He is a man formed by a particular tradition, Eton, the Royal Navy, and the clubs of St James's, yet trained to kill efficiently and without sentiment. When the polished manner falls away and the thuggish behaviour his profession requires is revealed, the effect is all the more unsettling for the contrast. It is far more disturbing than watching a thug who has never pretended to be anything else.

Bond's polished gentlemanly qualities are essential because they throw his ruthlessness into relief. I have already acknowledged that Sir Roger Moore's films depart from the novels; most Bond films take liberties with Fleming's work. However, Moore himself possessed the requisite polish and charm. When he turned nasty it was a shock to those taken in by his charm, pointing his Walther at the double agent Rosie Carver in Live and Let Die; interrogating Lazar in The Man with the Golden Gun by threatening to shoot him in the groin; threatening to break Miss Anders's arm; or, in For Your Eyes Only, kicking Locque from a cliff, he could switch off the charm and become a positively thuggish brute. That contrast is precisely what the part requires. Bond must be a light switch, night and day: two men in one. Without that duality, he is not quite Bond.

The levity of Moore's films often obscures this aspect of his performance. Consequently, people may scoff when one argues that Moore's Bond, despite the films' many departures from Fleming, is closer to the novelist's gentleman-and-killer than is commonly supposed.

Sir Sean Connery, George Lazenby, and Pierce Brosnan each conveyed that duality. In my view, however, Timothy Dalton came closest to capturing all the aspects of the character. His Bond is a polite gentleman who, once the switch has been flipped and he has been crossed, will feed a henchman to a shark in revenge, a scene found in Fleming's Live and Let Die, omitted from the 1971 film, and echoed in Dalton's Licence to Kill. Yet he will also spare an amateur female sniper who is, in fact, a cellist in The Living Daylights, explaining that he kills only professionals. Dalton's Bond is impatient with bureaucracy and weary of his work, as though he has been at it for far too long. His performance captured all the quintessential elements of the character.

If the intention of the reboot was to offer a grounded, realistic portrayal of Bond, the filmmakers ought to have looked to Timothy Dalton.

Daniel Craig's Bond, by contrast, lacks the gentlemanly aspect of Fleming's character. The man who can move through a casino or country house without attracting the wrong sort of attention is missing from Craig's portrayal. His Bond is rather more a Jason Bourne-ified David Callan.

Anyone familiar with Edward Woodward's series Callan will understand what I mean. Callan is a hard-edged government operative, entirely indifferent to polite social graces: not a gentleman spy.

I think Daniel Craig would have made an excellent Callan, and I enjoy all five of his films. I simply do not enjoy them in quite the same way as the original twenty Bond films, in which Bond's duality of character was present.

I hope that clarifies my point for those who think that I hate Daniel Craig. I do not.

Craig just isn't the gentleman who's a killer, Mr Kiss Kiss Bang Bang.

text:
Brian Kelly interviewed for the Maryland job, On3's Pete Nakos reports, and if he gets it, LSU might be happier than Maryland. LSU fired Kelly in October 2025 and, after a legal fight, agreed to pay his full buyout, about $54 million. But there's a catch in his contract. He has a "duty to mitigate," meaning he has to make a real effort to find another football job, and whatever that job pays comes off what LSU owes him.

Here's how that plays out. If Maryland hires him, LSU only owes the difference between his new salary and what's left of the buyout. Kelly makes about the same money either way. Maryland gets a coach with a long track record, and LSU gets a discount on the most expensive firing it has ever made. Every dollar Maryland pays Kelly is a dollar LSU doesn't have to.

Getting here was messy. LSU fired him after a home loss to Texas A&M, then told his lawyers it thought it had grounds to fire him for cause, which would have wiped out the buyout. Kelly sued within hours. A few weeks later LSU's president put it in writing that Kelly was fired "without cause" and would get the full amount, as long as he keeps looking for a coaching job. He's been calling games for CBS since.

Maryland's own buyout works the opposite way. The Terps fired Mike Locksley on Oct. 21 after a 2-5 start and 12 straight Big Ten losses. He went 39-54 in eight seasons and is owed close to $10 million, with half due in a lump sum within 60 days, according to Front Office Sports. His deal has "no mitigation or offset obligations," so Maryland pays all of it no matter where Locksley ends up.

Kelly can coach. He's 200-76 at Central Michigan, Cincinnati, Notre Dame and LSU, went 34-14 at LSU and has talked up Maryland's recruiting area and facility upgrades on TV this season. The real questions are that he's 65 and whether a program that's lost 20 of its last 22 Big Ten games is a job he wants. His contract lets him say no to offers that aren't comparable without losing the buyout.

Nothing's done yet. Interim coach Aazaar Abdul-Rahim is finishing the season, and other names are in the mix. My read: if Maryland hires Kelly, LSU should send flowers. They'd win the deal without ever making an offer.

The New Jersey Hallmark Christmas Towns Road Trip takes you to ten of the state's most charming towns, where historic streets, sparkling lights, and old-fashioned Christmas traditions bring the holiday season to life! 

🎄Clinton, NJ
🎄Morristown, NJ
🎄Lambertville, NJ
🎄Princeton, NJ
🎄Red Bank, NJ
🎄Ocean Grove, NJ
🎄Haddonfield, NJ
🎄Collingswood, NJ
🎄Historic Smithville (Galloway, NJ)
🎄Cape May, NJ

Start in Clinton, where the famous Red Mill provides a beautiful backdrop for Christmas decorations, Victorian carolers, and the Festival of Trees. In Morristown, the historic town green comes alive with thousands of lights, Santa's house, and holiday train rides. Lambertville offers decorated storefronts, cozy cafes, and beautiful old buildings along the Delaware River. Princeton's Palmer Square features a towering Christmas tree covered in thousands of lights, surrounded by festive shops and garlands. Red Bank welcomes you with glowing trees, decorated streets, and holiday shopping, while Ocean Grove's Victorian homes and quaint seaside streets add an old-fashioned Christmas feel. Haddonfield brings candlelight shopping, wreath-covered storefronts, and historic charm, while nearby Collingswood shines with more than 250,000 Christmas lights. Historic Smithville is especially magical, with over 120 illuminated Christmas trees floating on Lake Meone, dancing to holiday music. Finish in Cape May, where grand Victorian mansions, Christmas trolley rides, decorated inns, and Congress Hall's Winter Wonderland make for an unforgettable Christmas getaway.

text:
It’s kind of insane to me that social media platforms have been aware of the problems with their algorithms for years and have done virtually nothing to address them. If anything, the exploitation of these platforms by foreign (particularly authoritarian) regimes to manipulate public opinion has gotten worse.

The more absurd, racist, inaccurate, hateful, and conspiratorial a post is, the more engagement it generates. Russia, China, Qatar, and the Islamic Republic of Iran understand this well. That is why they invest enormous resources in media and social media manipulation through bots, sock puppet accounts, paid influencers, media outlets, and countless other methods. But there is something even more disturbing happening here…

Foreign interference doesn’t just involve creating false narratives from scratch. Authoritarian regimes are focused on identifying and amplifying narratives that already exist within Western societies. They exploit legitimate grievances, political divisions, and existing controversies, amplifying the most extreme voices until fringe positions appear mainstream. This is much harder to combat… Which brings me to the other major problem: influencers.

Unfortunately, the response to the destructive behavior of these foreign agents of chaos has largely been for domestic opportunists to join in, while tech platforms, media networks, and political leaders do virtually nothing about the self-destruction of Western civilization being accelerated by foreign regimes.

This is an enormous strategic mistake that has helped create a massive influx of grifters on every side of virtually every political issue.

People who suddenly realized they could financially profit from tragedy, war, political polarization, and human suffering are now dominating conversations they have no expertise in and often have absolutely nothing to do with. Some are being paid to push particular narratives. Others are simply chasing engagement because outrage has become a business model.

We have created an information ecosystem in which the incentives of authoritarian propagandists, domestic political grifters, and social media companies increasingly align. That is a national security vulnerability, not merely a cultural problem.

Authoritarian regimes want to destabilize the West, undermine trust in democracy, and exacerbate internal divisions. Political grifters want clicks, followers, money, and attention. Social media companies want engagement.

We created a system in which all three benefit from the exact same destructive behavior.

Meanwhile, instead of tech platforms taking a step back and asking, “Maybe we should rein this in?” the situation just keeps getting worse. And as my friend @talk2trav always says, the influencerization of everything is killing society. I couldn’t agree more.

We’ve created an entire class of people whose primary qualification for influencing public opinion is their ability to attract attention. Not knowledge. Not expertise. Not accuracy. Not even basic intellectual honesty. And somehow we’ve decided these people deserve enormous influence over politics, international affairs, public health, national security, and virtually every other issue of consequence.

Worse, traditional media outlets increasingly reward this behavior by treating follower counts as a substitute for credibility. It’s an absolutely absurd way to organize public discourse.

We’ve built an information economy that financially rewards the very behaviors hostile foreign governments are actively trying to encourage.

Instead of recognizing that as a profound strategic vulnerability, we’re celebrating the people who are exploiting it.

This is not a recipe for a healthy, successful, happy, or productive society. It’s a recipe for societal decay. If we don’t fundamentally rethink what we’re rewarding, who we’re elevating, and how these platforms operate, we’re going to keep allowing our adversaries to exploit our own systems against us

Last night, while thousands of Americans were stranded on airport floors, Pete joked at a Denver political conference about meeting people at the hotel bar and claimed "this should not be about politics." True leaders own their failures instead of spinning them for their next campaign.

For four years, Pete focused on DEI, ESG, and his political ambitions while core infrastructure decayed:

• 𝟏𝟗𝟖𝟎𝐬 𝐅𝐀𝐀 𝐓𝐞𝐜𝐡: Left the aviation backbone on 1980s copper lines and outdated routers, causing Friday's nationwide ground stop.

• 𝐃𝐄𝐈 𝐎𝐯𝐞𝐫 𝐌𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐭: Sidelined qualified aviation graduates amid the leaked answer key scandal, fueling a 3,800 controller shortage.

• 𝐍𝐞𝐠𝐥𝐞𝐜𝐭 𝐨𝐧 𝐭𝐡𝐞 𝐆𝐫𝐨𝐮𝐧𝐝: Left over 3,200 safety grants stalled and offered a single photo op visit after Hurricane Helene while warning I 40 would take years to rebuild.

Since Day One, Transportation Secretary Sean Duffy has been fixing the mess:

• 𝐌𝐞𝐫𝐢𝐭 𝐅𝐢𝐫𝐬𝐭: Shut down DOT DEI offices, audited past hiring scandals, and hired a record 2,235 new controller trainees.

• 𝐅𝐀𝐀 𝐎𝐯𝐞𝐫𝐡𝐚𝐮𝐥: Secured $12.5 billion to start replacing analog systems and demanded $50 billion more from Congress to finish the job.

• 𝐑𝐚𝐢𝐥 𝐚𝐧𝐝 𝐇𝐞𝐥𝐞𝐧𝐞 𝐑𝐞𝐥𝐢𝐞𝐟: Cleared the 3,200 grant backlog, boosted rail safety enforcement, slashed red tape to reopen I 40 fast, and delivered $2.9 billion in highway relief for North Carolina.

America does not need politicians chasing DEI, ESG, and their next campaign. We need builders like Sean Duffy who show up and get the job done. 🇺🇸✈️🛣️

text:
Florida Governor Ron DeSantis has signed the Florida SAVE Act, requiring all new, renewed or replaced driver’s licenses and state IDs to display a holder’s citizenship status starting January 1, 2027.

Under the law, licenses for U.S. citizens will clearly indicate their status, while non-citizens, including legal permanent residents, will have the letters “NC” for “Not a Citizen” printed on their cards.

State officials say the measure is meant to improve verification of citizenship for government and voting-related purposes. Current licenses remain valid until their normal expiration date, and once a non-citizen becomes a U.S. citizen, the state will issue a free replacement card.

Critics, including Escambia County Democratic Party Chair Derrick Scott, warn the designation could open the door to discrimination, particularly during traffic stops.

Supporters counter that the card simply offers another way to identify a person’s legal status. The law has already drawn legal challenges and warnings from civil rights groups, even though most of its provisions will not take effect until after this fall’s midterms.
