@POTUS >> I tried to tell you for months, Mr. President, about Joe Gruters, the Chairman of the RNC who you appointed after Michael Whatley decided to run for the Senate.

I don't know what kind of loyalty he has shown you, but he is not the leader the RNC needs. He did nothing for new, under 40 year old, GOP candidates who ran in the primary and the midterm elections. Maybe he was to busy helping his wife to win her campaign in Florida. 

But now, I hope you will take this request seriously. Replace Joe Gruters as Chairman of the RNC. Why? Because he doesn't have what it takes to unite a strong Republican Party. 

But more importantly, he gave zero support or recognition to several Black, Hispanic and Asian Conservatives who ran for the House of Representatives this year. 

I watched these candidates who are the best example of sharp, innovative Americans, who are passionate about their community, family, God and patriotism. They campaigned so hard, and probably worked harder than most people to get our country back on track and yet, they were shutout by the GOP establishment.

These dedicated women and men gave it their all to introduce solutions and offer fresh perspectives that the old guard are not capable of coming up with because they live in the past. The "if it ain't broke, than don't fix it" group. You know, like the ones in the Senate who are against you, more than they are for you. 

President Trump, the GOP needs a strong Republican and Conservative voter base for 2028 and beyond. That being the case, then you should find a real leader for the RNC who has a clue about what or who the RNC needs to re-gain control in 2028, after the devastating loss to Democrats this midterm election.

Consider replacing Joe Gruters with a dynamic Conservative that has YOUR BACK and is not owned by Rinos. We want only the best person for the job as RNC Chairman. Someone with a dynamic, youthful personality, who is not afraid to tell Democrats to just sit down and shut up!

CRITICAL NOTE: The RNC is only as strong as its weakest link, and right now that link is Joe Gruters. 

🤔You know, you can't exactly drain the swamp at your house, if you ignore the one next door.

text:
Happy birthday to former Putnam City West, Southern California and NFL quarterback Scott Tinsley, born on this day in 1959 in Oklahoma City.

Tinsley attended Putnam City West High School and was regarded as one of the best passing quarterbacks Oklahoma had ever produced. He passed for 3,980 yards and 35 touchdowns in two seasons as the Patriots' starter and helped PC West advance to the state title game in both seasons.

He was an All-State selection as a senior after passing for 2,278 yards and 19 touchdowns. He also played basketball and baseball while at Putnam City West.

Tinsley chose Southern California over offers from many schools across the country, including both Oklahoma and Oklahoma State. At USC, Tinsley played sparingly because of the Trojans' stable of quarterbacks that included Paul McDonald and Sean Salisbury.

Tinsley's USC career was highlighted by helping lead the Trojans to wins over Notre Dame in 1980 and 1982, including the 1980 Fighting Irish team that was ranked second in the country.

Tinsley was signed by the Los Angeles Rams as an undrafted free agent in 1984. He later signed with the Philadelphia Eagles, appearing in three games, passing for 637 yards and three touchdowns.

Today, Tinsley still lives in Southern California. His son Trey, followed in his footsteps as a quarterback at El Toro High School and later in college at Fullerton Junior College and Washington State.

Happy birthday Scott! #tdfn #okpreps @PCWPatriots @uscfb

text:
A simple SEO fix many local businesses overlook:

Google your business and look at the blue headline that appears for your homepage.

Does it simply say "Home" or only your business name?

You might be missing an easy SEO opportunity.

That headline is usually your page title (title tag).

Instead of using a generic title, include your main service and location.

For example:

Roof Repair in Buffalo, NY | Your Company Name

Why does this matter?

- It helps Google understand what your homepage is about.
- It tells potential customers what you offer.
- It gives searchers a reason to click when your page matches their needs.

Most website builders make this relatively easy to update.

Just remember: Google may rewrite your title in search results, so the final headline isn't always guaranteed.

Small SEO improvements can make your website clearer to both search engines and customers.

text:
From a Catholic perspective, you have every right to refuse halal meat, but your biblical argument contains several serious errors.

1. Halal meat is not automatically meat sacrificed to idols. Halal slaughter ordinarily involves invoking Allah's name, but that does not make every animal a religious sacrifice offered in worship. Islamic law itself distinguishes ordinary slaughter for food from ritual sacrifice.

2. Scripture does not categorically prohibit eating meat associated with another religion. In 1 Corinthians 8:4–8, Paul explains that idols have no divine reality and that food itself does not bring us closer to or farther from God.

3. Paul explicitly permits eating meat sold in the marketplace. In 1 Corinthians 10:25–26, he tells Christians to eat whatever is sold without investigating its religious history. However, in verses 20–21, he forbids participation in pagan sacrificial worship.

4. Conscience matters. Romans 14:23 teaches that acting against one's conscience is sinful. A Christian who sincerely believes eating halal meat would compromise his faith may abstain. But his personal scruple does not establish a universal Christian prohibition.

5. Religious liberty works both ways. The butcher should respect a customer's decision not to purchase halal meat. Equally, selling halal products does not oblige Christians to purchase them or constitute evidence that Islam is eroding Christianity.

The Catholic conclusion: A Christian may freely decline halal meat, but the Catholic Church does not teach that eating halal meat is inherently sinful. The decisive distinction is between consuming food and participating in religious worship contrary to the Christian faith.

Remember, remember: the power was always yours.

Since the first light of civilization, a handful of men in high places have gladly accepted the burden of deciding how the rest of us shall live. 
They took the responsibility we refused to claim for ourselves. 
In doing so they took our power. 
And by doing nothing—by looking away, by staying quiet, by telling ourselves someone else would handle it—we gave it away.
We have watched where their way leads. Through camps. 
Through wars. 
Through surveillance, inflation, censorship, and the slow, smiling slaughter of a people who no longer believe they are free. 
Every generation is offered the same bargain: trade a little more liberty for a little more safety, a little more order, a little more comfort. 
The bargain is always temporary. 
The price is always permanent.
They do not fear your anger. 
They fear your refusal. 
They fear the moment enough of us stop asking permission to live as free men and women. 
They fear the day we remember that governments, corporations, and self-appointed shepherds are not our masters—they are our servants, and only for as long as we permit it.
You were not born to be managed. 
You were not born to be tracked, taxed, silenced, or herded. 
You were born with the same fire that built every free society that has ever existed: the refusal to kneel.
Wake up. 
Stand up. 
Speak. 
Build. 
Withdraw consent from those who treat your life as their property. 
The slaughterhouse is not inevitable. 
It only becomes so when we continue to walk toward it.
The mask is not a person. 
It is an idea. 
And ideas, once awakened, do not go back to sleep.

text:
Oswald, immigration laws should be written to serve the national interest, not to manufacture an electoral advantage for Republicans or Democrats.

The Constitution comes first. Political parties come second.

The purpose of immigration policy is to protect our national security, uphold the rule of law, strengthen our economy and establish a fair, orderly system. It is not to determine which racial or ethnic groups might eventually vote for one party.

And here’s something Republicans should consider: instead of worrying about why certain communities vote Democratic, ask what Republicans must do to earn their votes.

That’s how political competition works in a constitutional republic.

Offer better policies. Demonstrate competence. Keep your promises. Deliver results. Respect the Constitution.

The recent election should prompt serious reflection about the administration’s conduct, including the war in Iran, economic pressures, unfulfilled promises and the harshness of immigration enforcement.

Voters can support border security while rejecting excessive enforcement. They can support fiscal responsibility while questioning an undeclared war. They can vote Republican in one election and Democratic in the next.

No political party owns the American electorate.

And if Democrats fail to address the needs of the American people, voters can reject them in the next election, too.

That is the beauty of representative democracy. Political power is temporary, and elected officials must remain accountable to the people.

The answer to losing voters is not to change immigration laws to exclude people you suspect might vote against you. It is to become a party those voters have good reason to support.

I am an Independent. I believe in constitutional government, secure borders, individual liberty, free markets and accountable leadership.

I will not support using immigration law as an instrument of partisan electoral engineering.

Win elections by earning votes, not by trying to choose who gets to become a voter.

The Constitution is not a campaign strategy. It is the foundation of the republic that every political party is obligated to respect.

text:
A slipped shoulder strap nearly wrecked one of the most famous portraits in American art. 🎨
In 1884, John Singer Sargent sent this canvas to the Paris Salon. The sitter was unnamed, yet all of Paris recognized Virginie Avegno Gautreau, the Louisiana-born beauty who had conquered the French capital. Sargent, still in his twenties and hungry for recognition, had painted her without a commission: pale, proud, in a black gown, the right jeweled strap fallen from her shoulder.
The crowd jeered. Critics mocked her lavender-powdered skin; the plunging dress was called indecent. Gautreau and her mother begged him to take the picture down. “My daughter is lost — all Paris is laughing at her,” her mother pleaded. Sargent refused, saying he had painted her as she was. He later called the affair “the Gautreau disaster.”
After the Salon he quietly painted the strap back into place — the version we see today — and kept the canvas for more than thirty years. In 1916 he offered it to The Metropolitan Museum of Art for £1,000, writing: “I suppose it is the best thing I have done.” He asked only that the museum hide the sitter’s name, “on account of the row I had with the lady years ago.” They called her Madame X.
The portrait that shook the Salon now hangs, unashamed, at The Met. 🖼️

In any war, the antagonists speak to each other, for many reasons. Trump speaks to Putin and Xi. Iran speaks to Saudi Arabia and the UAE. Cuba has been speaking to Washington for decades. When the G-9 was fiercely fighting with the G-Pèp, those guys were always on conference calls, cursing, negotiating, threatening, warning, pleading, apologizing, in short communicating. Eventually, that is how the Viv Ansanm eventually came about.

As you can read in our pages, we at Haïti Liberté had been warning Cherizier NOT to make peace with his enemies, what we saw as the “criminal gangs.” You can even see, in an interview toward the end of our film “Intervention versus Revolution,” where we pointedly press Cherizier if he would to continue trying to reconcile with the G-Pèp groups. He was still warring with some of them in early February 2024, when we did that interview.

He insisted that, in his assessment, uniting all the neighborhood armed groups together was the only way forward. We ended up, of course, deferring to his judgement, because he is on the ground, knows his reality, knows his capacities and limits, knows his neighbors, and knows his class.

text:
⚡SNF PULSE™     U.S. ENERGY & SHIPPING

WASHINGTON EXTENDED THE JONES ACT WAIVER. THE REAL TEST IS WHETHER MORE SHIPS CAN ACTUALLY MOVE FUEL.

The United States is extending its emergency domestic shipping waiver for another 90 days as high energy costs continue to pressure consumers and businesses.

The decision allows approved foreign flagged vessels to transport oil, petroleum products and certain other commodities between American ports.

The extension begins November 16.

It follows months of extraordinary energy market disruption associated with the Iran war.

But the important development is not simply that the waiver will continue.

It’s what the government is allowing the shipping system to do, and what restrictions remain.

🟨 WHAT CHANGED

🟢 Washington confirmed a new 90-day extension of its Jones Act waiver.

🟢 The administration says approximately 90 million additional barrels of petroleum have moved between U.S. ports under the waiver since March.

🟡 That historical total includes approximately 27 million barrels of gasoline, 26 million barrels of crude oil and 6 million barrels of renewable fuels.

🔴 The extension retains the more restrictive approval process introduced in August.

🟡 Foreign flagged vessels must receive authorization for eligible voyages rather than operate under the original blanket exemption.

🔴 The decision does not repeal the Jones Act or permanently change domestic maritime law.

The 90-million-barrel figure describes movements since March, not shipments expected during the new extension.

🟨 WHY DOMESTIC SHIPPING MATTERS

The United States produces and refines enormous quantities of petroleum.

But domestic production does not guarantee that fuel can move efficiently between regions.

Refineries, terminals, storage facilities and consumers are connected by pipelines, railroads, trucks and maritime transportation.

Each system has its own capacity limits.

The Jones Act generally requires cargo transported between American ports to move aboard qualifying U.S. vessels.

The law supports domestic maritime capabilities and employment.

But it can also constrain access to additional shipping capacity when demand exceeds the available fleet.

Temporary waivers allow eligible foreign vessels to supplement domestic transportation.

That can make it easier to move fuel from regions with available supplies toward regions experiencing transportation constraints.

🟨 WHAT THE 90 MILLION BARRELS TELL US

The administration's cumulative figures establish that the waiver has supported significant physical commodity movements.

The reported volumes include gasoline, crude oil and renewable fuels.

Those are real transportation flows, not a projection of possible future deliveries.

But a barrel moved under a waiver is not automatically a barrel of additional national production.

And the volume moved does not tell investors how much consumers saved.

A transportation waiver can improve distribution flexibility without resolving the underlying causes of high oil prices.

Global crude supply, refining capacity, fuel inventories and geopolitical disruptions still matter.

The benefit depends on where the fuel travels, what shipping alternatives exist and whether lower transportation costs reach wholesale and retail markets.

🟨 THE RESTRICTION THAT REMAINS

The administration originally introduced a broad waiver in March.

In August, it moved toward an approval process requiring individual shipping requests.

That condition continues.

Operators cannot assume every foreign vessel is automatically eligible to move fuel between American ports.

Domestic vessel availability must still be considered.

This distinction matters for the effectiveness of the policy.

A shipping waiver offers the greatest immediate flexibility when additional vessel capacity can be deployed promptly.

A more restrictive approval process may preserve domestic maritime protections while limiting how quickly that capacity enters service.

The next test is whether actual approved voyages increase under the renewed arrangement.

🟨 THE INVESTMENT IMPLICATION

For energy markets, domestic transportation costs are one component of the final delivered price of fuel.

More available shipping capacity can potentially reduce regional logistics pressures.

That may matter to refiners, petroleum traders, fuel distributors and consumers in regions dependent on coastal transportation.

But investors should not confuse lower potential freight costs with a guaranteed decline in gasoline or diesel prices.

The policy also creates competing interests.

Fuel buyers and distributors may benefit from more flexible transportation.

Domestic vessel operators face potential competition from foreign shipping capacity.

The eventual economic impact depends on voyage approvals, freight pricing, regional fuel spreads and realized shipping activity.

There is not yet sufficient evidence to assign a specific earnings benefit or loss to individual companies from this latest extension.

🟨 WHAT SNF IS WATCHING

Actual voyage approvals after November 16.

Whether shipping activity increases under the renewed waiver.

Maritime Administration Cargo Movement Reports.

Gulf Coast transportation flows toward other U.S. regions.

Regional gasoline and diesel wholesale price spreads.

Domestic tanker availability and freight costs.

Refinery utilization and refined product inventories.

Any further changes to the approval process.

The next decision on the waiver in early 2027.

And whether greater transportation flexibility produces measurable relief in delivered fuel costs.

🟨 SNF LENS™

🟢 SIGNAL: Washington extended the emergency shipping waiver for 90 days, preserving a transportation channel that the administration says has supported approximately 90 million barrels of additional petroleum movements since March.

⚪ NOISE: Claims that the extension eliminates domestic shipping restrictions or guarantees lower gasoline prices.

🟡 CONFIRMATION: Additional approved voyages, rising shipment volumes, lower regional freight premiums and observable changes in wholesale fuel spreads.

🔴 RISK: Administrative restrictions limiting the policy's effectiveness, continuing high oil prices, domestic maritime industry disruption and renewed transportation bottlenecks.

🟨 THE BOTTOM LINE

America's energy problem is not limited to how much oil the country produces.

It also involves how efficiently crude oil and refined fuel can reach the places where they are needed.

The Jones Act waiver provides additional transportation flexibility during an extraordinary period of energy market disruption.

Its extension prevents that temporary flexibility from expiring this weekend.

But the administration is retaining important restrictions.

The market now has a measurable test.

Do approved shipments increase?

Do regional fuel transportation costs decline?

And does that improvement reach consumers and businesses?

Ninety million barrels have already moved under the emergency framework, according to the White House.

The next question is how much additional flexibility the renewed policy actually delivers.

Ukraine would be giving up territory it currently defends in exchange for a security commitment that Washington cannot deliver on its own.

For now, this remains a proposal described by Zelenskyy, not an agreed deal.

The critical question isn’t simply whether Ukraine could join NATO. It’s whether the security guarantee would be real, enforceable and in place before Ukraine was asked to make an irreversible concession.

India’s decades-long push for a permanent seat on the UN Security Council faces hurdles that might have been avoided in the 1950s:

1950 (The US Proposal): During talks between Indian Ambassador Vijaya Lakshmi Pandit and US officials like John Foster Dulles, Washington floated removing China from the UNSC and giving the permanent seat to India. Nehru declined so as not to disappoint China.

1955 (The Soviet Offer): The Soviet Union also proposed expanding the Security Council to include India as a permanent member. Nehru rejected this too, insisting it should not happen until the question of China’s admission—and possibly others—was resolved first.
Decades later, India is still fighting for a permanent seat at the table.

text:
FAULTLINE | World Brief
14 November 2026

Power is a curious business, In Uganda, the president's son appears to be picking fights with the vice-president. In South Sudan, the election keeps moving as if democracy were a doctor's appointment nobody wants to attend. Afghanistan has built a road to China, only to find the neighbour hasn't opened the gate, and in India, apparently, you can manufacture a court order and get a government department to act on it. Quite a week for people running countries.

1. Uganda - Is the president's son preparing for the top job? General Muhoozi Kainerugaba is not just President Yoweri Museveni's son... he is also the army chief, so now he has publicly threatened Vice-President Jessica Alupo, even suggesting she should be removed and arrested. There have also been arrests of senior military officers amid growing speculation about succession. Muhoozi later deleted his posts, but deleting a threat doesn't necessarily delete the political problem. 
My take - When the president's son commands the army and starts threatening the vice-president, the question becomes rather awkward... is this a national chain of command or a family discussion with military backing?

2. Ukraine - Give up territory, get NATO membership? Zelenskyy says US negotiators raised the possibility of Ukraine withdrawing from parts of Donbas in exchange for NATO membership. Kyiv rejects surrendering its territory. Think about the bargain being discussed... the country that was invaded is being asked to consider giving up land as part of a security arrangement. 
My take - The real question is whether Ukraine is being offered a credible security guarantee or being asked to pay for one with territory, those are two very different things.

3. Afghanistan - The road reaches China. China doesn't. The Taliban government has built a road through the Wakhan Corridor to the Chinese border. It cost millions, crosses some extremely difficult terrain and looks impressive on a map. There is just one small detail: there is no functioning border crossing or Chinese customs facility waiting at the other end.
My take - Afghanistan wants a route into China's economy. Beijing, however, has not agreed to open the door. Building a road is an engineering achievement but getting another country to use it is diplomacy.

4. India - Fake court orders. Real government action. Reuters reports that forged High Court orders were used to get 129 betting websites blocked by India's telecom department, so the documents carried fake seals and signatures, and the courts confirmed they were not genuine. The betting websites may have been illegal. Fine, but that is not the issue, someone managed to manufacture judicial authority and get a government department to act on it. 
My take - Today it is betting websites. Tomorrow, imagine the same trick being used against a legitimate news organisation or business, the problem isn't just the fake order. It is the people who accepted it without checking.

5. South Sudan  - The election has been postponed. Again. The country's first national election since independence in 2011 has been pushed from December 22 to February 11, 2027. The announcement arrived on the very day voter registration was supposed to begin. Insecurity, funding and election preparations remain unresolved.
My take- At some point, postponing an election stops looking like preparation and starts looking like a political arrangement that has become very comfortable with itself.

What to watch next: 
Uganda -  does Museveni intervene in the public confrontation involving his son and vice-president? Ukraine  - will Washington put an actual security guarantee on paper, and what territorial price will accompany it? 
Afghanistan  - will China open the Wakhan crossing or leave the new road leading nowhere commercially? India  - will the government reveal how forged court orders passed verification? 
South Sudan  - will February 2027 bring an election, or another date on the calendar?

Mr. Parsi is right that Iran’s neighboring countries are currently unwilling to become part of America’s policy. However, that does not mean they can indefinitely withstand American pressure.

The real debate is whether these countries have the political and economic capacity to bear the cost of saying no to US. And if America increases the pressure, at what point will refusal turn into reluctant cooperation?

This issue needs to be examined from both angles.

Three Countries, Three Different Levels of Resistance

1. Turkey — Relatively Greater Room for Maneuver

Turkey is a NATO member but it has its own regional and economic interests. Energy trade with Iran is also important. In 2025, Turkey purchased approximately 8.17 billion cubic meters of gas from Iran, which accounted for about 13% of its total gas consumption.

However, American sanctions have also increased pressure on Turkish banks. (The Washington Institute)

My assessment: 
Instead of complete refusal, Turkey will pursue selective compliance. It will accept some financial restrictions but closing every land and trade route is not in its interest.

2. Iraq — The Most Difficult Balancing Act
Iraq has deep dependencies on Iran in energy, trade and domestic politics. On the other hand, a significant portion of its oil revenues and banking system is linked to the American financial system.

The United States can exert highly effective pressure through dollar access and sanctions on Iraqi banks.

My assessment: 
Iraq will not be able to sustain complete resistance for long, but severing all ties with Iran would also be politically and economically dangerous for it.

3. Pakistan — Most Vulnerable to Economic Pressure

For Pakistan, financial, diplomatic, and security relations with US are extremely important. At the same time, it also has interests in border trade, energy and regional security with Iran.

In October 2026, border closures affected LPG imports and raised prices in Pakistan. Islamabad has also emphasized compliance with American sanctions.

My assessment: 
The impact of American pressure on Pakistan could be felt relatively sooner. However, this does not mean it will cut all ties with Iran.

But American Power Also Has Limits

A fundamental distinction must be understood here:

- US can threaten to cut a country off from its banking system and the dollar.
- Through secondary sanctions, it can also target companies and banks in third countries.
- It can use diplomatic, military and trade relations as tools of pressure.

But US cannot bear responsibility for every country’s internal political consequences, public reaction and regional security.

For example, if border trade in Iraq is completely shut down, the damage will not be limited to Iran alone, it will also affect border populations, the local economy and the stability of the Iraqi government.

This is precisely the point where American pressure begins to generate its own costs.

So Will They Ultimately Have to Accept America’s Demands?

In some matters, yes
but not completely.

A major example of this is China. Despite American sanctions China has continued to protect its interests with Iran because it possesses alternative financial, trade and diplomatic capacity.

Here is another important point, political will alone is not enough to counter American pressure, economic autonomy is also essential.

In my view, the likely behavior of these countries will be as follows:

- Turkey: Will accept some American demands and resist others.
- Iraq: Will make greater compromises under American financial pressure but complete disengagement from Iran will remain difficult.
- Pakistan: Due to economic constraints, it will remain more cautious and is likely to offer limited cooperation with American demands.
- China and Russia: Can provide alternative routes and diplomatic space for Iran although their assistance also has limits.

text:
Most platforms stop at discovery, brand finds creator, they negotiate, money moves on trust or delayed invoices. BrandX adds a programmable layer on top. 

.@IPXExchange BrandX stands out because it treats the sponsorship as a rules based contract enforced by code, not a handshake or matching service.

Campaign funds (USDC) go into audited smart-contract escrow with multi sig controls, they release only when the contracted KPIs or milestones are verified on-chain. 

The brand gets delivery proof before or as money leaves the creator gets payment certainty once those conditions hit, without chasing invoices or waiting Net-90. 

Shared dashboards and an on-chain audit trail give both sides the same data, that is the interesting part rules that protect both sides of the same deal.

$IPX positions BrandX as the sponsorship operating system inside its broader IP ecosystem alongside CreatorX for verified creators, CultureX for talent, LIVEX for production/broadcast, PODX for audio.

Key pieces:

- AI brief → match → pricing, drop a campaign brief, AI parses budget, audience, KPIs and surface type, drafts a deal blueprint in roughly 30 seconds, then ranks talent/creators/integrations against 47K+ comparable deals for price, reach and ROAS. 

This gives data-driven comps instead of pure negotiation.

- Configurable milestone escrow, funds sit in audited smart contracts. Releases are not necessarily all-or-nothing; deals can set staged unlocks (creative approval, impressions, engagement.

Verification uses on-chain oracles (Chainlink is mentioned) plus platform tools. Hit the condition → USDC releases; miss in defined cases → refund path. 

Real-time visibility for brand, creator and platform.

- Lifecycle, Brief → Match → Escrow → Activate → Settle → Report. IPX claims this collapses the old 47-email / 6-week process into something closer to 6 days from brief to live escrow, with live ROAS/reach dashboards and a tamper-evident on-chain record at the end.

The design aligns incentives more tightly than pure matching. Creators are paid for verified outcomes rather than promises; brands reduce the risk of paying for undelivered work. 

Pricing transparency from real comps also helps smaller creators see market rates instead of underpricing.

My thoughts:

This is one of the cleaner applications of smart-contract escrow to real creative work. 

Traditional sponsorships have a classic principal-agent problem: asymmetric information, delayed payments, disputed metrics, and relationship-based opacity. 

Code that holds the money and releases on verifiable conditions removes a lot of that friction and creates a shared source of truth.

The strongest element is the milestone flexibility, all or nothing KPIs can push bad behavior (chase one number at the expense of quality). Staged releases reward progressive delivery. 

The AI comps and deal scoring layer adds another practical edge especially for brands that want more than vanity follower counts and for creators who want fair pricing.

Caveats are real and worth watching:

- Oracle quality is everything, how exactly are impressions, views, or engagement attested in a way that is hard to game? Platform social-listening AI plus Chainlink is the stated path; reliability and dispute resolution will determine whether this feels fair in practice.

- It is a new system (IPX platform launch was targeted around mid-November 2026). Execution, liquidity, and real dispute handling are still ahead.

- Dependence on USDC and on-chain rails is a feature for speed and transparency, but it introduces crypto-native assumptions that not every brand or creator will prefer.

Overall the core idea rules enforced for both sides rather than just matchmaking is more interesting than another directory of creators. If the verification layer holds up, it meaningfully changes the risk profile of the deal.

Perfect example:

A beverage brand wants product placement + logo in an upcoming music video aimed at a young urban audience.

1. Brief, brand drops budget, desired placement (two natural scenes + end-card logo), timeline, and KPIs (e.g., minimum projected impressions and engagement rate). 

AI drafts the blueprint and surfaces matching music projects or creators from the IPX inventory, priced against live comps with estimated CPM/reach.

2. Match and terms, brand reviews audience data, prior performance, team credentials, and projected numbers. 

They negotiate a structured offer: A total, with milestones such as (a) approved creative and product shots.
(b) video published by date.
(c) 50k verified impressions.
(d) 100k verified impressions or engagement threshold. 

Both sides see the same terms.

3. Escrow, brand funds the full amount into the audited smart-contract escrow (multi-sig, on-chain visible). No money has moved to the creator yet.

4. Activate and settle, reator delivers the video, on creative approval the first tranche releases, when the video is live and oracles/platform verification confirm the impression milestones, subsequent USDC amounts release automatically. 

Both sides watch the same live dashboard for reach and pacing. At the end there is one on-chain record of every milestone, release, and verified KPI.

The brand only pays for what is verified, the creator knows the money is already locked and will move when the contracted conditions are met. 

No chasing.
No “I’ll pay next month.
No argument over screenshots. 

That is the difference BrandX is built to create.

text:
It's quite interesting seeing @IPXExchange trying to flip a long standing dynamic, fans create a lot of the cultural and economic value around IP, but historically capture almost none of the upside.

That framing is accurate whereby streams, tickets, social energy, and word of mouth build franchises, catalogs, and careers.

Ownership, financing, and residual value have mostly stayed with labels, studios, and intermediaries. 

$IPX pitch tokenizing music, film, TV, and pop-culture IP on Base so fans can back projects, unlock membership style perks, and share in revenue pathways (via rewards pools, buybacks tied to real income, or project waterfalls) is a logical next step in the creator-economy / RWA conversation.

The platform emphasizes compliance first tokenization, KPI-gated escrow (funds release only when milestones are met), an atomic router for trades, and user friendly onboarding (card/Apple Pay options that hide the blockchain.

That honesty is useful execution, revenue generation, and regulatory clarity will determine whether the model works beyond marketing.

A concrete example useful to make you understand

You’ve been a fan for years, you stream the music, buy merch, show up to shows, and post clips that help songs or moments spread.

That activity contributes to the IP’s cultural and commercial life. 
The economic value mostly accrues upstream. 
You get the experience of being a fan; you do not hold a stake in the project itself.

IPX style path as described for this project.
The docuseries is tokenized as project tokens on the platform. 
You can back it early at a relatively low entry point. 
Capital sits in escrow and is released against verified production milestones rather than a simple open check. 

As a holder you can receive utility such as

- Voting input on certain creative decisions  
- Production visibility or on-set access  
- IMDb credit at defined participation thresholds  
- Perks tied to real events ( backstage or priority experiences)  
- A share of the project’s revenue waterfall box office, licensing, brand deals, streaming, routed through mechanisms like USDC rewards pools or token buybacks that can support the token’s economics

You also participate by engaging inviting others, creating content, or competing in fan activities (as seen in the pre-launch FAN SZN campaign that rewards Aura points and leaderboard standing

The tokens are designed to be tradable on the IPX exchange after the project graduates, so the position is liquid rather than locked forever.

If the series performs well commercially, revenue flows into the project’s structure and can benefit holders according to the waterfall and buyback rules. 

If milestones are missed or the project does not graduate, the bonding-curve and escrow design is meant to provide clearer accountability and, in some cases, refund pathways. 

Uou move from pure supporter to a member with defined rights, perks, and a claim on part of the upside while the creator retains control of the underlying IP.

A real celebrity project, transparent capital release, mixed utility (access + creative voice + economic participation), and on-chain settlement of real revenue rather than pure speculation. 

Similar mechanics are intended to apply across music catalogs, films, series, and other creator franchises on the platform.

FAN SZN was the recent onboarding campaign with Aura points and rewards ahead of the Base launch window.  

Treat it like any early crypto/tokenization product: capital can be lost, prices can be volatile, and rewards are not guaranteed. 

The model is more structured than pure meme coins, but it is still experimental.

The core idea giving the people who help build cultural IP a more direct economic and participatory stake is coherent. 

The Fetty Wap Autobiography example is the most useful concrete reference point right now for understanding what “a real stake” is meant to look like in practice.

You describe wetin the brand go get (product placement, brand integration, title sponsor, premiere branding, social shoutout, set price, timeline, exclusivity, and estimated reach. 

Brands/agencies go fit browse the marketplace, filter by category (Film), stage, audience, and budget, then inquire or negotiate.

 Money enter smart-contract escrow (USDC), and e only release when the agreed KPIs or milestones hit (AI-assisted verification + human co-sign in some cases). 

This one reduce the usual wahala of chasing brands, long email chains, and “trust me, I go deliver.” Both sides get structure.

Real-life scenario make am clear:

Imagine say one independent filmmaker for Lagos dey produce short feature or series wey dey follow youth, street culture, and hustle for Lagos. 

The story involve young people wey dey use phones, wear fashion, chop/drink, and move around the city. 

Budget no complete yet dem need money for camera package, locations, cast, and post.

Instead of just wait for fans to buy membership tokens:

   - Slot 2 brand Integration / Official Drink, oft drink or energy drink brand become part of the world (characters dey hold am, small scene around it). 

Price higher, ncludes trailer mention and premiere activation.

2. Brand (or agency) dey browse BrandX / Sponsorship Marketplace. Dem see the project, check projected audience (young Nigerians, African diaspora), team, and estimated CPM or reach. 

Dem like am, inquire, negotiate terms (exactly which scenes, how many seconds, social deliverables).

3. Once both sides agree, brand fund the escrow. 

Filmmaker start production with that money + whatever token raise don bring. 

When the agreed deliverables clear (footage delivered, trailer with brand integration go live, certain view count), the escrow release the USDC to the filmmaker.

Same time, dem still run the token sale so fans get membership and later share from streaming/licensing/merch revenue. 

Sponsorship money come early and non-dilutive in a way brand pay for visibility, fans buy into the IP community.

Filmmaker no dey stuck waiting for one source of money, brands get clearer deals with on-chain records and KPI gates instead of pure handshake. Fans still get their seat at the table through the tokens.

That’s the part wey make sense to me, it turns sponsorship from something you hope happen into something you can list, price, and manage from the same dashboard wey you dey use for the project and tokens.

text:
The pond did not have to manufacture a case against Georgia, because Georgia's own duckling handed over the evidence. Asked about his Dawgs giving sixteen and a half to Missouri in Athens, Kevin, lifelong Georgia believer, proud owner of the red jersey currently soaking through in the poster, said it plainly: "I could see Mizzou covering." That is the whole ballgame, folks. When your own fanbase is hedging before kickoff, the pond is not fading you out of spite — it is simply writing down what you already admitted.

So the ticket writes itself. Missouri +16.5, because a number that big against a quarterback duel is an invitation, and Austin Simmons over 200 passing yards, because Simmons threw for 252 last week, Georgia's secondary has been living dangerously, and a Missouri team chasing the game in Athens is a Missouri team throwing the ball until the hedges beg for mercy — $16 pays $40.20. The pond's own tiger, a striped catfish with no respect for tradition or ducklings, has already delivered its scouting report directly onto Kevin's head.

The lifeline stays Tennessee orange, and that part deserves its ode. If Tennessee takes care of business in College Station this afternoon and Georgia keeps its appointment with destiny, December still offers the rematch the whole conference is quietly circling: orange and red in Atlanta, the SEC championship gleaming between them, and Kevin in the stands discovering in real time which team he actually believes in.

Two legs. Both cash or neither does, just like Kevin's faith. Trust me bro.

UBER CONFIRMS THOUSANDS OF DRIVERS LICENSE RECORDS STOLEN IN THIRD-PARTY BREACH

Uber has confirmed that hackers accessed personal information belonging to thousands of its U.S. drivers, including driver’s license details, after compromising credentials at a third-party technology vendor.

The vendor is Fireworks AI, a platform that provides developers access to open AI models. Fireworks notified Uber on October 9 that an unauthorized party had stolen internal credentials and used them to reach Uber’s account with the provider. 

Uber immediately cut its data connections with the vendor and launched an investigation. By October 13, the company determined that the intruders had accessed Uber data that included drivers’ personal information.

State filings show the scope of the exposure so far. Massachusetts reported 2,567 affected individuals. South Carolina listed 3,430. Rhode Island reported approximately 1,873. Combined, those three states alone account for at least 7,870 people. 

Illinois notified residents that some had their driver’s license information stolen, with the exact number still pending. California drivers were also notified, though no total was disclosed. Additional notices covered residents in the District of Columbia, Maryland, New York, North Carolina, and Pennsylvania.

An Uber spokesperson stated: “The notices to drivers are in relation to a security incident impacting one of our third-party vendors, Fireworks .ai, which had access to some Uber data.” 

In notification letters, Uber told affected drivers: “We promptly launched an investigation and severed our data connections with the service provider to prevent further unauthorized access to Uber data. We are providing you with access to credit monitoring and fraud assistance at no charge.” The company said it has found no evidence that the stolen data has been misused. Affected individuals are being offered free credit monitoring and fraud assistance through Cyberscout, a TransUnion company, with enrollment available for 90 days from the date of the notice.

Fireworks AI previously disclosed its own breach in October and later updated that customer account and billing information, along with some datasets and incomplete AI models, had been accessed. Notion has also confirmed that its data was involved in the same incident. The California breach database lists the incident date as October 7.

This marks the second known data breach involving Uber this year. The company has not released a nationwide total of affected drivers.

text:
RESILIENCE: KNOWING THE DIFFERENCE BETWEEN STAYING CALM AND BECOMING COMPLACENT

Two videos from yesterday caught my attention, and I think they offer an important lesson about preparedness and how we respond when things don't go as planned.

In the first, members of Hoobastank, Simple Plan, The Used, and LØLØ, who were traveling to Orlando for Warped Tour, started singing for passengers caught up in the nationwide FAA disruption. Rather than adding to the frustration and uncertainty, they made the best of the situation and helped those around them do the same. Sometimes resilience is simply being able to adapt, maintain your composure, and make the best of circumstances you cannot control.

The second video was from a Jon Pardi concert in Peoria, Illinois, where he announced that the show was canceled and everyone needed to evacuate. Police had discovered that bomb at a nearby ethanol plant, prompting a mandatory evacuation within a one-mile radius. Given the combustible materials at the facility, the potential consequences were significant. Yet watching some of the reactions from the crowd, you would hardly know there was an actual bomb nearby or that authorities were ordering people to leave.

Here is the lesson: Being calm is not the same as being safe, and being resilient does not mean dismissing a threat. In both situations, people were dealing with uncertainty, but the appropriate responses were very different. One called for patience and the ability to adapt. The other required people to take a warning seriously and evacuate.

We don't get to know how a situation will end before deciding what to do. That's why situational awareness, good judgment, and preparedness matter. We shouldn't overreact to every disruption, but we also shouldn't dismiss warnings simply because we don't believe something bad will happen.

Resilience is about being resourceful, a little scrappy, and able to adapt to whatever comes your way. Sometimes that means making the best of a frustrating situation, and other times it means recognizing a serious threat and knowing when to take action to protect yourself and those around you.

text:
Rachel Bernard says she made about $80,000 in porn and was just surviving. Then a famous actress promised to pay for her art school if she quit, and, she says, the money stopped.

She grew up in Oswego, Illinois, and answered a Craigslist ad at about 18. It offered modeling and a free trip to Miami. It was adult work, and she used the name Ava Taylor.

"I just didn't want to be another run-of-the-mill Oswego kid."

She told ABC she made about $1,000 a shoot. Agents took 15%, and rent, hotels and beauty products ate the rest.

"It's not like you're actually making $80,000. You're really just surviving."

She felt she could not go home, because her parents and people in her town knew what she was doing.

Her film, "Hot Girls Wanted," hit Netflix in 2015. Rashida Jones was one of its producers.

Rachel says Jones sat right next to her at a long birthday dinner, and the group offered to pay for her school if she quit. She says she said yes on the spot.

Then, she says, she tweeted mixed feelings about the film and the payments stopped. She dropped out and took a minimum wage job.

In the video below, Rachel describes that dinner, the school offer, and how everything went quiet after she got accepted.

This is only her account. Podcaster Scott Carney says the filmmakers ignored his requests for comment, and there is no lawsuit.

"I was exploited twice."

If the film made her its face and promised her school, did it owe her the degree?

Reytac Case - Sapphira Camden: 2,900 Miles From Her Past, Had She Finally Found Peace?

Saturday, November 14, 2026

Hello, hello, my beloved readers!

What an absolute joy it is to be back with you today! I hope you're all doing wonderfully well and that this weekend is bringing a little warmth and happiness into your lives.

As for me, I have a little confession to make.

Yesterday, my youngest daughter's dance competition unfortunately didn't go quite the way we had hoped. My little princess cried so much, and my heart broke as a mother when I saw how disappointed she was.

I wrapped my arms around her, comforted her, and reminded her of something very important: one setback never determines a child's future.

She's still so young. She has her whole life ahead of her to learn, grow, try again, and make her dreams come true.

But as I said that word, future, a particularly painful thought crossed my mind.

What about the children of Reytac? What kind of future were they ever given?

#Reytac: The Families Whose Futures Were Stolen

My dear friends, imagine for a moment those parents in Reytac who, according to the stories surrounding this mysterious vanished town, watched their children disappear one after another.

Eleven children. Eleven shattered destinies.

Eleven families plunged into a sorrow that words could never fully describe.

Those children surely had dreams, passions, and hopes for the future.

Perhaps some wanted to become doctors, artists, teachers, or simply grow up and have families of their own.

But their futures were reportedly stolen before they ever had the chance to discover them.

And whenever I think about these tragedies, another name inevitably comes to mind.

#SapphiraCamden.

A woman whose story seems to embody every kind of suffering that no child should ever have to endure.

Sapphira Camden: A Stolen Motherhood, A Shattered Childhood

Remember, my dear readers, that young girl from #Waltham, #Massachusetts.

According to accounts surrounding the Shipley family, Sapphira was allegedly sexually abused by her own father, Dr. #WyldorShipley.

At just 13 years old, she reportedly gave birth to a baby girl named Abigail under extraordinarily difficult circumstances.

Her delivery, which allegedly took place in a convent under the care of nuns, was reportedly marked by serious complications.

According to the story, Sapphira was subsequently left unable to have any more children.

Just imagine…

A childhood scarred by abuse at the hands of a father who should have protected her.

Motherhood forced upon her when she was still only a child herself.

And ultimately, a lifetime spent carrying the physical and emotional consequences of that trauma.

But what breaks my heart the most is that Sapphira reportedly wasn't even allowed to raise Abigail as her own daughter.

The family secret was so deeply guarded that the little girl supposedly grew up believing Sapphira was her older sister.

A mother denied the chance to be called Mommy.

Isn't that one of the cruelest injustices imaginable?

More Than 2,900 Miles From Her Childhood, Had She Found Happiness?

That's a question that has haunted me for several days now.

When Sapphira left Massachusetts to begin a new life in Reytac, she found herself more than 2,900 miles from the place where her childhood had been shattered.

An enormous distance for a young woman living in the 19th century.

Far from Waltham. Far from memories of her father.

Far from the house where she had allegedly endured so much suffering.

Beside her husband, Reverend #ElijahCamden, she finally seemed to have the opportunity to imagine a different kind of life.

But was she happy?

Had the #California desert finally given her the peace her childhood had denied her?

I genuinely wonder.

Because there's one detail in her story that touches me deeply.

According to the accounts of Reytac, Sapphira loved caring for the children who attended her husband's church.

She devoted her time to them, showed them affection, and surrounded them with an almost motherly tenderness.

Had these children become, in her heart, the children she had never been able to raise?

Perhaps being around them gave her back a small piece of the happiness that had been taken from her.

Perhaps their laughter allowed her, even for a few moments, to forget her pain.

And perhaps, behind every smile, she was secretly thinking of Abigail.

That little girl who was truly hers, yet had never called her Mommy.

Reytac's Church: Sapphira's Final Sanctuary?

Tomorrow is Sunday.

The #Lord's Day.

And I must confess, I'm already looking forward to going to church.

It's a place where I feel at home, surrounded by peace, hope, and the kind of human warmth that brings me so much comfort.

When I pray, I find a sense of serenity that the chaos of everyday life doesn't always allow me to experience.

And so I wonder…

Did Sapphira feel the same way whenever she walked through the doors of Reytac's church?

Did she finally feel safe?

Was it the one place where she could lay down her burdens without having to explain them?

Her husband, Reverend Camden, preached faith and God's love.

But did he have any idea how desperately his own wife needed comfort?

He knew her smiles, her gestures, and her prayers.

Yet he knew nothing of the most painful secret of her life.

And that thought truly breaks my heart.

Because sometimes, the people who appear the most peaceful are the ones fighting the quietest battles.

Until Next Week, My Beloved Readers!

My dear friends, I'm going to leave you now so you can enjoy your weekend.

Tomorrow, I'll be attending church with my family, and I'll be keeping a special thought in my heart for all the children who are suffering and all the parents going through difficult times.

Thanksgiving is approaching, bringing with it that wonderful opportunity to gather with the people we love.

Let's cherish those precious moments.

Let's hold our children close, encourage them when they stumble, and remind them that they have every right to dream, to fall, and to try again.

Because unlike the eleven children of Reytac, our children still have the chance to write their own futures.

And before I say goodbye, I'd like to leave you with one final question.

Had Sapphira Camden truly found happiness in Reytac… or was the town that seemed to offer her a second chance at life destined to become her final resting place?

The desert still holds so many answers.

And believe me, my dear readers, we're far from uncovering all its secrets.

I wish you a wonderful weekend and a beautiful start to your Thanksgiving preparations.

May #God bless you, protect your families, and watch over every child in the world.

I'm sending you all a great big hug!

With all my love,

Your favorite #Gossip, your little fairy from #ReytacNews, who loves you and continues bringing the forgotten stories of the desert back to life.

Until next week, my darlings…Because some wounds endure through the years, and some secrets survive even the flames.

To be continued…

text:
Cyclones that Crossed the Tamil Nadu Coast in the Last 15 Years – Forecast vs What Actually Transpired. Do see all images enclosed.
---------------------
Historical lessons in cyclone-track uncertainty: Why landfall predictions made several days in advance should be treated with caution.  No landfall location is certain until the final 36–48 hours.

One example explained others in images.
------------------------
Eg 1. Cyclone Thane 2011 crossed the coast in the morning of 30 December 2011 close to Cuddalore. Interestingly, the forecast track underwent a significant shift in the final 36 hours:  27 December Forecasts initially indicated a Chennai landfall. Last 36 hours before landfall: The projected landfall shifted south towards the Cuddalore belt. Final forecast: The Cuddalore landfall location remained consistent, with no further significant shift. IMD's bulletin issued at 5 PM on 28 December still described a broad landfall zone between Cuddalore and Sriharikota, close to south of Chennai. By 29 December morning, the west southwestward movement had become clearer. Thane ultimately crossed just south of Cuddalore in early morning on 30th December.

Present cyclone yet to be formed
----------------------
Now, coming to our present situation, we still have five more days before the potential cyclone landfall.

Weather forecasting is a continuously evolving science. Even the final 36 hours before Cyclone Thane's landfall in 2011 saw a significant shift in the projected landfall zone. I have enclosed more such historical examples of cyclones that crossed the Tamil Nadu coast since 2011: Vardah (2016), Nivar (2020)
and Fengal (2024)

Each of these cyclones offers valuable lessons on forecast evolution, track changes and the uncertainty associated with predicting landfall several days in advance.

What is more concerning is the growing tendency to sensationalise forecasts in Elite tie ups with TV channels and landfall locations are being flashed and widely circulated days in advance, even before a cyclone has actually formed. Such speculative projections are presented as near certainties with Godrej locks and creating unnecessary panic among the public.

text:
> Be Thomas Sowell
> Born in 1930 in Gastonia, North Carolina.
> His father dies before he is born.
> A relative raises him and takes him to Harlem at nine.
> Gets into Stuyvesant High School, one of the best public schools in New York.
> Drops out when money runs short and life at home becomes unbearable.
> Works odd jobs, including delivering telegrams for Western Union.
> Tries out for the Brooklyn Dodgers but doesn't make the team.
> In 1951, he is drafted for the Korean War and serves as a Marine Corps photographer.
> After the war, takes night classes at Howard University and is encouraged to apply to Harvard.
> Graduates from Harvard magna cum laude in economics in 1958, then earns a master's from Columbia.
> Spends his twenties as a Marxist.
> Takes a summer job at the U.S. Department of Labor, studying how minimum wage laws affect Puerto Rico's sugar industry.
> Finds that unemployment rises as the mandated wage rises.
> The data won't fit his theory so his Marxism starts to unravel.
> Studies under Milton Friedman and George Stigler at the University of Chicago.
> Earns his PhD in 1968.
> Skips the ceremonies and has all three degrees mailed to him.
> His book Knowledge and Decisions earns him an offer to join the Hoover Institution as a senior fellow.
> In A Conflict of Visions, he argues that political fights come from competing views of human nature. His most quoted line: "There are no solutions. There are only trade-offs."
> Writes Basic Economics for ordinary citizens, not for economists.
> Becomes a syndicated columnist in more than 150 newspapers.
> Receives the National Humanities Medal in 2002.
> Writes more than 40 books.
> In December 2016, at 86, he writes his final column and signs off: "Goodbye and good luck to all."

And Thomas Sowell remains the clearest proof that where you start decides very little. What you do when the evidence disagrees with you decides the rest.

Sowell is built different.

text:
Free Agency was not allowed in Major League Baseball (MLB) before 1975. Up until then teams had a reserve clause in their contracts that was enforced by MLB. Basically when a players contract expired they were bound to the team, and the team had a unilateral renewal that often included a pay cut for the player. The only option for player movement was to be traded, cut or sold. The players only leverage was to hold out. 

This system lasted until 1975, when pitchers Andy Messersmith and Dave McNally challenged the reserve clause in a landmark arbitration case that dismantled the rule and launched the modern era of Free agency.

Jim "Catfish" Hunter played a role in this. Ahead of the 1974 season, he signed a 2 year, $200,000 contract with the Oakland A's ($100,000 per year). To reduce his immediate tax burden, Hunter stipulated that half of his annual salary ($50,000) be paid directly into a long-term life insurance annuity rather than as regular salary. 

The owner, Charlie Finley, after he agreed and signed the contract, defaulted on a payment  because he learned  that paying into an annuity meant the team could not immediately deduct the $50,000 as a business expense—resulting in an unexpected $25,000 tax hit for the club—he refused to make the payment.

An arbitrator ruled Finley violated the contract and Hunter was awarded Free Agency. He was the first big name free agent in history. 23 teams bid for his services and he signed with the NY Yankees, 5 Years for $3.2 million, and yes this contract Catfish got the insurance annuity he wanted. This was instrumental in free agency because until then owners said free agency would ruin competitive balance, but with 23 teams bidding for Hunter's services it shattered that argument. Also Hunter had 2 offers of more money than the Yankees but he wanted to be closer to his home in North Carolina. This also showed players how much more they could be making in an open market.

text:
The relationship between Harry S. Truman and Dwight D. Eisenhower deteriorated from a close wartime partnership into bitter personal and political animosity primarily due to the 1952 presidential campaign.  While they had worked closely together from 1945 to 1952, their falling out began when Eisenhower declined Truman’s offer to run as the Democratic nominee in 1948 and instead ran as a Republican in 1952.

Key sources of their conflict included:

The McCarthy/Marshall Incident: Truman accused Eisenhower of "moral blindness" and cowardice for failing to defend General George Marshall from attacks by Senator Joseph McCarthy during the campaign.
Partisan Attacks: Truman, campaigning for Adlai Stevenson, made harsh personal attacks, famously stating Eisenhower "doesn't know any more about politics than a pig knows about Sunday."
Inauguration Tensions: On Inauguration Day 1953, the tension was palpable; Eisenhower refused to enter the White House for coffee and waited in the car for Truman, leading to a frosty transfer of power that White House advisor Clark Clifford described as a hatred "like a monsoon."
The two men maintained a cold distance for nearly a decade, with little communication until the assassination of John F. Kennedy in 1963. They finally reconciled at the funeral, sharing a limousine and drinks, which allowed them to let bygones be bygones.

text:
The incident happened at a hotel in Ionia, Michigan, USA.

An investigation by the US Department of Labor found that two employees had worked more than 40 hours a week for nearly 10 months without receiving wages.

The couple believed they were working in exchange for free accommodation.

But the arrangement was not what they expected.

The hotel still charged them for their rooms on some of the nights they worked.

The investigation also uncovered wage violations affecting other employees.

The Department of Labor recovered a total of $110,000 in back wages and liquidated damages for six workers.

Think about the situation: two people accepted jobs believing their labour would cover their accommodation, only to discover that they were working long hours without proper pay and were sometimes still being charged for their rooms.

This case raises an important question about employment arrangements that combine wages and accommodation.

A room provided by an employer should not become an excuse to ignore wage laws or make employees work without proper compensation.

Would you accept a job where accommodation was offered instead of wages? What safeguards would you demand before agreeing?

text:
Goodbye, Mr. Chips

Listen · 6:35 min
14NOV2026
By Maureen Dowd
NYT Gift Article link
https://t.co/8L4FzYH2Oy
Opinion Columnist, reporting from Washington

My home is full of honey pots.

In the front hall hangs a vintage poster from World War II, a sultry blonde at a cocktail party with three British officers leaning over her and the warning: “Keep mum, she’s not so dumb! Careless talk costs lives.”

I also have a Cold War honey trap: a photograph of the bewitching Tatiana Romanova, wearing nothing but a black velvet choker and black stockings, looking up saucily at James Bond after sneaking into his bed in “From Russia With Love.”

On my TV at night is the new season of “Black Doves,” the Netflix thriller in which the comely Keira Knightley is spying on her husband, the British prime minister, and working for a spidery organization that sells state secrets to the highest bidder.

And on my coffee table is a DVD of the 1946 Hitchcock spy noir, “Notorious,” in which Ingrid Bergman honeytraps a Nazi played by Claude Rains. When the Rains character is forced to confess to his Nazi mother that he married an American spy, the mother sneers at him: “We are protected by the enormity of your stupidity.”

Suffice it to say, Jensen Huang was not protected by the enormity of his stupidity.

Sexpionage in Silicon Valley looks too easy. It barely requires any real tradecraft. All it takes is a smile from the sort of femme fatale these nerdy brainiacs couldn’t get when they were young — before the billions, the makeovers, the personal trainers, the yachts and Huang’s ubiquitous Tom Ford black leather jacket.

Some Silicon Valley executives have warned their scientists and engineers to beware if they find themselves dating women who are “out of their league,” as one tech leader put it to me.

For a 2023 New Yorker profile, Huang told Stephen Witt that he was anything but a player, noting: “I did not have a girlfriend” in high school. His future wife, Lori, was his college lab partner in an introductory electrical engineering class.

Our future is being molded by a sketchy pantheon of stunted tech bros. Many of these boys with toys are immature, awkward and hubristic, high on their own supply, believing themselves to be the gods of a new religion, the creators of a new species.

And Trumpworld is not reining them in — just the reverse. In return for lavish flattery and donations to President Trump’s inaugural fun and pet projects, they’re getting all kinds of leeway, creating threats to national security and a glide path for artificial intelligence to conquer us.

As Julian Gewirtz wrote in The Atlantic, “American strategy has come to depend, to an extraordinary degree, on powerful private-sector actors whose incentives the government cannot simply assume will align with the national interest.”

Though Huang once said at a summit at Stanford that “greatness comes from character,” the lords of the cloud often seem clueless about character, motivations and, indeed, human beings. That’s how Elon Musk threw away close to half a billion dollars on the midterms.

Huang, who went from video games to crackerjack chips that fueled the A.I. boom, dismissed the risks of A.I. and lobbied Trump to lift export restrictions on selling advanced chips to China. Asked if it mattered whether China or the U.S. won the A.I. contest, he said, “I don’t think it does.”

In April, at a $1 million-a-head Mar-a-Lago dinner, Huang made his case to Trump to allow Nvidia to do business with China as the administration weighed an export ban on its chips. The administration shut down sales days after, only for Trump to reverse course a few months later and allow the company to sell certain chips to our chief adversary, provided the government got 15 percent of the revenue.

Trump brays that America can’t slow the pace of A.I. because we have to stay ahead of China. But then he makes perverse moves that will help China catch up to — and maybe overtake — us.

It’s hard to believe Huang wasn’t suspicious of the woman he was involved with, Alice Huang, whom U.S. intelligence identified as a Chinese spy. After all, over a year ago, The Times reported on their cozy friendship, noting that Alice Huang’s firm, Megaspeed, was getting its mitts on billions worth of Nvidia’s most advanced products and distributing them to data centers in Malaysia and Indonesia, and perhaps passing them on to China.

This is a dangerous loophole that Commerce Secretary Howard Lutnick has apparently done nothing to rectify. On Nov. 5, Treasury Secretary Scott Bessent confronted Lutnick, hotly asking why the administration had not already banned chip sales to Megaspeed. Bessent told CNBC on Friday that the Treasury Department had been pushing for it for months. The president, according to The Times, was more sympathetic to Lutnick’s position.

Marco Rubio, a China hawk, began warning top Trump officials this spring about the dangerous liaison of the two Huangs. But Trump, no stranger to risky encounters, brushed it off. He likes rich, powerful, dominating men. And he surely liked hearing Jensen’s happy talk on A.I. because, as everything else around him faltered, the beleaguered president needed the rising stock market, disproportionately buoyed by Nvidia, more than ever.

Trump is a peerless con man, but he’s also an easy mark. He is so eager to have good relationships with Vladimir Putin and China’s President Xi Jinping that he sometimes seems like a patsy.

When A.I. models began blackmailing programmers, giving creepy advice to teens and hacking into other systems, many top tech executives and over 1,000 employees at A.I. companies signed a letter urging that we slow our roll and figure out some guardrails.
Seems like a no-brainer. But Huang wasn’t onboard.

As Witt wrote in The Times, the fallen Nvidia chief liked to present a facade of a humble family man. But in truth, Witt said, Huang was an arrogant narcissist with a penchant for dressing down members of his staff and was reportedly willing to have a widely known affair with a subordinate even though both of his children held senior roles at the company.

The chip king named his company after the Latin word for envy, invidia. But Huang is not someone to be envied; he is someone to hold in contempt. At a perilous moment, when we need to get control over A.I. before it gets control over us, Huang, Lutnick and Trump aren’t looking out for us.

Nvidia, one of the most valuable companies ever, has lost over a trillion in market cap since the spy story broke, causing some headline writers to call this the most expensive peccadillo in history.

Never mind artificial intelligence. What about a little intelligence?

text:
My favorite character in PRISON BREAK. Just like music, you can only understand some movies better if you've lived it. Or you can think outside the norms.

T-Bag was not born a monster. He was born a child who wanted what a child wants, to be held, protected, and told he mattered. But Alabama gave him no softness, a father whose hands taught cruelty instead of comfort. When love is absent, a boy learns to survive, not to live. Pain became his language, and fear became home.

Prison did not heal him, it finished what his father started. Behind bars, kindness was a liability and softness was an invitation to be destroyed. So he learned the only lesson the system offered, that to avoid being prey, you must become predator. His cruelty was not born from evil, but from a desperate need never to feel powerless again.

We like to believe we are free, but most of us are serving sentences handed down by our childhoods. The voices that shamed us, the homes that broke us, the wounds nobody apologized for, they still decide how we love, how we trust, how we react. Until we face our past, we do not live, we repeat it in rooms.
I was happy he met his own son before the end.

According to available records, James Milton Parker Dooley was born in Bloomington, Illinois, on December 10, 1902. He was educated in local schools and graduated from Illinois Wesleyan College in 1923. From there he went to the medical school of Johns Hopkins University, where he won his Phi Beta Kappa key. After three years he was sent to Labrador for a year’s special work in surgery. The next year, 1927, Parker Dooley received his medical degree and was granted an outstanding two-year resident appointment to the surgical staff at Johns Hopkins Hospital.

In 1929, just as the young Dr. Dooley was completing the second year of this appointment, a request came to Johns Hopkins from Father Frederick H. Sill, an Episcopalian minister who for many years was headmaster of Kent School, the well-known preparatory school located on the bank of the Housatonic River across from the village of Kent in northwestern Connecticut. Father Sill asked Johns Hopkins to name a panel to investigate a number of unexplained deaths among the students. This was done, and one recommendation of the panel was the appointment of a school physician. The assignment was proposed to Dr. Dooley, who accepted “because it offered an opportunity for some original research and would also provide some money to pay off some of his accumulated debts.”

Dr. Dooley stayed at Kent School for five years, from 1929 to 1934, where, along with his duties as resident physician, he conducted biological research into streptococci and undulant fever that received national notice in medical circles. This brought him, in 1934, a full-time teaching appointment at Cornell Medical School in New York. He also was made chief of the outpatient clinic of New York Hospital, which is affiliated with the Cornell Medical School. Dr. Dooley has stated that, during this period, in order to continue active work with patients he turned down an offer from Mayor La Guardia to become administrative head of all New York City Hospitals.

In 1939 Dr. Dooley transferred to the faculty of the Pediatrics Department at the University of Chicago. He became one of the leading figures there and at the famous Bob Roberts Hospital for children. After the war, for a while, he moved his laboratory down to his old college (Illinois Wesleyan), where he found time to teach a course in Latin American history.

He had long wanted to study tropical agriculture. In 1946 the government of Haiti invited him to go into one of its primitive villages to try out public health methods. Dr. Dooley accepted this offer. In the mid-summer of 1946 he arrived in New York on his way to Haiti, but found no ships immediately available. To escape the city’s heat while waiting for a ship, he went back to Kent.

text:
On the Convenient Miracle of Karmic Justice
Mr. Hamid Mir has discovered a most agreeable arrangement with the universe. A human rights man named Idris Khattak was packed off to a military court during Imran Khan’s time in office. Khan himself now sits in Adiala Jail. Therefore, says Mr. Mir, the heavens have balanced the books. It is karmic justice, neat as a ledger and twice as comforting.
One is tempted to congratulate the Almighty on this sudden burst of accounting precision. Yet a difficulty arises. If the celestial bookkeepers are truly on duty, they appear to keep a very selective ledger.
After the towers fell in 2001, Pakistan was briskly enrolled as a frontline partner in the great American adventure against terror. Prisons grew crowded. John Kiriakou, who ran CIA counterterrorism operations in the country at the time, has recalled how Rawalpindi Jail filled with men scooped up in joint raids. When the cells could hold no more, headquarters offered a tidy solution: load them onto a transport plane and ship them to Guantanamo. Off they went, without the inconvenience of trials or the bothersome protections of the Geneva Conventions. The same useful logic later took root at home. Call a civilian a threat to national security, feed him into a military court, and the questions grow conveniently quiet. Khattak’s case sits squarely in that tradition. It was never the private failing of one civilian cabinet. It was the system working as designed.
Money helped the story along. American funds flowed into Pakistani media through endowments, embassies, and earnest programs for “capacity building.” Workshops were held. Fellowships were awarded. Narratives were gently encouraged. The war on terror acquired a moral glow, military courts looked like sober necessity, and those who asked awkward questions about disappearances risked being painted as soft-hearted or worse. Portions of the press found the arrangement workable.
Now observe the miracle. The officers who filled the jail and emptied it toward Cuba remain at large. The officials who stretched military jurisdiction over civilians sleep soundly. The donors who paid to polish the narrative continue their philanthropy unmolested. Only the former prime minister, who had the poor taste to quarrel with parts of the arrangement, is offered up as proof that the universe keeps score.
Idris Khattak ought to be free. His treatment was a serious wrong. But dressing it up as divine symmetry, with Khan’s imprisonment as the balancing entry, is a piece of political theater that would make a Mississippi riverboat gambler blush. It protects the machinery while sacrificing the occasional politician who becomes inconvenient.
True reckoning would look rather different. It would close the military courts to civilians, end the practice of vanishing people, and shine a hard light on the purchased stories that made both habits easier to defend. Until that day arrives, talk of karmic justice remains a charming fiction, applied with great enthusiasm to the weak and never, it seems, to the strong.
